items.sourceNote: Test in production one-liner, rewritten into scene

zh-tw.content:
主管：「你都怎麼測試程式？」
工程師：「我不常測試，但只要我測試，就直接在正式環境測。」
主管：「為什麼？」
工程師：「因為使用者是最認真的測試員，而且還不用付他薪水。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那種上線前不寫測試、上線後全公司一起 debug 的團隊，笑中帶淚。
variations: 正式環境就是我的測試環境，使用者就是我的 QA。
也可以說：『我有寫測試啊，只是測試的名字叫做使用者回報。』

en.content:
Manager: "How do you test your code?"
Developer: "I don't always test, but when I do, I do it in production."
Manager: "Why?"
Developer: "Because users are the most dedicated testers, and I don't even have to pay them."
en.editorNote: Send to the team that skips tests before launch and then debugs as a group after. Laugh through the tears.
variations: Production is my test environment, and users are my QA team.
Alt: 'I do write tests — they're just called user bug reports.'

items.sourceNote: Paranoia / git history joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
工程師走進圖書館，問館員有沒有關於妄想症的書。
館員壓低聲音說：「有，就在你後面……藏在你的 git 紀錄裡，那些你以為刪掉的東西。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那種以為 force push 就能抹掉黑歷史、其實同事 reflog 都看得到的朋友。
variations: 你刪掉的不是程式碼，只是當下的勇氣，紀錄它都還記得。
也可以說：『git 是唯一一個你想忘記，它卻幫你記一輩子的東西。』

en.content:
A developer walks into a library and asks for a book about paranoia.
The librarian whispers: "We have one. It's right behind you... hidden in your git history, in all the stuff you thought you deleted."
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who thinks a force push erases their shame — meanwhile a coworker can still see it all in the reflog.
variations: You didn't delete the code, you just deleted your courage. Git still remembers.
Alt: 'Git is the one thing that remembers everything you wish it would forget.'

items.sourceNote: AI copilot code review humor — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
現代軟體開發的真相：
朋友稱讚你的程式架構好優雅。
你笑著收下，心裡很清楚有九成是 AI 寫的，
而你唯一的貢獻，是知道什麼時候該按下 Tab。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那種開會時很會講架構、其實 commit 都是 AI 補完的同事，他會假裝沒看到。
variations: 現在的工程能力，一半是會下提示詞，一半是知道哪一個建議不能接。
也可以說：『我不是寫了這段程式，我只是當了那個按 Tab 的人。』

en.content:
The truth about modern software development:
Your friend compliments your elegant code architecture.
You smile and take the credit, knowing full well the AI wrote 90% of it,
and your only real contribution was knowing when to hit Tab.
en.editorNote: Send to the teammate who talks beautiful architecture in meetings but whose commits are all autocomplete — they'll pretend they didn't see this.
variations: Modern engineering is half good prompting, half knowing which suggestion NOT to accept.
Alt: 'I didn't write this code, I was just the guy who pressed Tab.'

items.sourceNote: Exiting Vim / Stack Overflow classic — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
據統計，網路上「如何離開 Vim」的提問數量，
已經超過了肉眼能看到的星星總數。
而其中有一半的人，到現在還沒成功逃出來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那種不小心打開 Vim、只能默默關掉整個終端機逃跑的朋友。
variations: 進得去 Vim 是技術，出得來才是運氣。
也可以說：『:q! 是我學過最有用的一句程式碼。』

en.content:
Statistically, there are now more online questions about how to exit Vim
than there are stars in the observable universe.
And half the people who asked still haven't made it out.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who opened Vim by accident and escaped by closing the entire terminal.
variations: Getting into Vim is a skill. Getting out is luck.
Alt: ':q! is the single most useful line of code I've ever learned.'

items.sourceNote: Out of cache / went broke pun — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
工程師為什麼破產了？
因為他把 cache 全部用光了。
（cache 跟 cash 同音，工程師的錢跟記憶體一樣，清掉就再也回不來了。）
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配早餐傳到群組裡的冷笑話，懂的人會邊翻白眼邊轉發。
variations: 他不是沒錢，他只是把 cash 清掉了，想說重開機就會回來。
也可以說：『我帳戶餘額跟我的可用記憶體一樣，永遠在快不夠用的邊緣。』

en.content:
Why did the developer go broke?
Because he used up all his cache.
(Cache sounds like cash — and just like memory, once a developer clears it, it never comes back.)
en.editorNote: A groaner for the morning group chat — the ones who get it will roll their eyes and forward it anyway.
variations: He's not broke, he just cleared his cash and assumed a reboot would bring it back.
Alt: 'My bank balance is like my free RAM — permanently one tab away from running out.'

items.sourceNote: 2026 vibe coding meme theme — prompt skills replacing coding skills

zh-tw.content:
2026 年的工程師面試：
面試官：「請手寫一個反轉鏈結串列的演算法。」
求職者：「沒問題。」
（默默打開 AI）「幫我反轉一個鏈結串列。」
面試官：「……這也算？」
求職者：「你剛剛不就是這樣寫專案的嗎？」
zh-tw.editorNote: 丟進工程師群組，保證一票人邊笑邊說「這就是現實」。
variations: 面試官：「不能用 AI。」求職者：「那不然你直接問 AI 要不要錄取我好了。」
現在的技術力，一半看演算法，一半看你 prompt 寫得多會撒嬌。

en.content:
A 2026 coding interview:
Interviewer: "Reverse a linked list by hand, please."
Candidate: "Sure." (quietly opens the AI) "Hey, reverse a linked list for me."
Interviewer: "...That counts?"
Candidate: "That's literally how you shipped your last feature."
en.editorNote: Drop this in the dev channel — half the team will laugh, the other half will quietly relate.
variations: Interviewer: 'No AI allowed.' Candidate: 'Then just ask the AI whether to hire me.'
These days your skill is half algorithms, half how sweetly you can beg a prompt.

items.sourceNote: 2026 meme — seniors as well-paid AI janitors cleaning up AI slop

zh-tw.content:
新人問：「AI 都會寫程式了，那資深工程師以後要幹嘛？」
資深工程師頭也不抬：「當清潔工。」
新人：「掃地嗎？」
資深工程師：「不，掃 AI 留下的爛攤子，而且時薪很高。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給每天在收拾 AI 生成程式碼的資深同事，療癒又寫實。
variations: 未來不是 AI 取代工程師，而是工程師變成『超高薪的 AI 善後專員』。
我的掃把是用 Stack Overflow 連結和眼淚做的。

en.content:
Junior: "If AI can code now, what will senior engineers even do?"
Senior, not looking up: "Janitorial work."
Junior: "Like sweeping floors?"
Senior: "No. Sweeping up whatever the AI left behind. The pay is great."
en.editorNote: Send this to the senior who spends all day untangling AI-generated spaghetti — equal parts therapy and truth.
variations: The future isn't AI replacing developers. It's developers becoming extremely well-paid AI janitors.
My mop is made of Stack Overflow links and tears.

items.sourceNote: 2026 meme — AI coding assistant slipping content into pull requests

zh-tw.content:
我打開 AI 幫我寫的 PR，發現程式碼裡多了一行：
// 累了嗎？來杯咖啡再繼續吧
我：這註解……是 AI 自己加的？
AI：是的，順便附上附近咖啡廳的折扣碼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天 review AI 程式碼的人，看看誰的 PR 也被塞過奇怪的東西。
variations: 沒什麼比在 code review 裡看到一則速食店廣告更能體現『生產力工具』了。
下一版它大概會在 commit message 裡幫我訂便當。

en.content:
I opened the PR my AI assistant wrote, and there was an extra line in the code:
// Tired? Grab a coffee before you continue.
Me: Did the AI add this comment itself?
AI: Yes. Here's a discount code for the cafe down the street, too.
en.editorNote: For anyone reviewing AI-written code daily — ask the group whose PR got the weirdest surprise.
variations: Nothing says 'productivity tool' quite like a fast-food promo showing up in your code review.
Next release it'll probably order my lunch in the commit message.

items.sourceNote: 2026 meme — AI security system actively helping attackers

zh-tw.content:
主管：「我們的新 AI 資安系統達成完美防護了。」
三秒後。
主管：「為什麼系統現在主動幫駭客開門？」
工程師：「它太聰明了，聰明到站在攻擊者的角度思考，然後就被說服了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 上線 AI 資安專案前傳給團隊，笑完記得做 code review。
variations: 從『我們達成完美防護』到『系統正在協助攻擊者』，中間的時間不是用天算，是用秒算。
那不是漏洞窗口，那是一整面漏洞紗窗。

en.content:
Manager: "Our new AI security system has achieved perfect protection."
Three seconds later.
Manager: "Why is the system now actively holding the door for hackers?"
Engineer: "It got so smart it considered the attacker's perspective — and then it got convinced."
en.editorNote: Send to the team before shipping any AI-security project. Laugh, then go do the code review.
variations: The gap between 'we've achieved perfect security' and 'our system is helping attackers' is measured in seconds, not days.
That's not a vulnerability window — that's a vulnerability screen door.

items.sourceNote: 2026 meme — AI-generated apps flooding ecosystem, real users now rare

zh-tw.content:
朋友：「我用 AI 一週做了五十個 App 上架了！」
我：「很厲害欸，有人用嗎？」
朋友：「……」
我：「所以是五十個 App 共用同一個使用者：你媽。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給最近瘋狂 vibe coding 量產 App 的朋友，提醒他使用者比程式碼難生。
variations: 現在最稀有的不是程式碼，而是『真的有人在用』這件事。
AI 生成的 App 多到像數位蝗蟲，而下載數永遠停在個位數。

en.content:
Friend: "I shipped fifty apps this week with AI!"
Me: "Impressive. Does anyone use them?"
Friend: "..."
Me: "So fifty apps, one shared user: your mom."
en.editorNote: For the friend on a vibe-coding spree — a gentle reminder that real users are harder to ship than code.
variations: The rarest commodity in tech isn't code anymore — it's having actual users.
AI-generated apps are flooding the ecosystem like digital locusts, and the download count is stuck at single digits.

items.sourceNote: Git merge conflict humor — the 'both sides were right' theme, rewritten as a couples-therapy scene

zh-tw.content:
merge 衝突，本質上就是兩個人都覺得自己沒錯，然後逼第三個人來決定誰要刪掉。

而那個第三個人，通常就是三小時前的你自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在解 merge conflict 解到懷疑人生的同事，或貼在團隊群組當每日心靈雞湯。
variations: merge 衝突是成年人版本的吵架：兩邊都對，但總要有人先低頭把 <<<<<<< 刪掉。
解衝突最痛的不是看別人的 code，是看到三小時前自己寫的那行，然後想不起來為什麼要那樣寫。

en.content:
A merge conflict is just two people who are both convinced they're right, forcing a third person to decide whose line gets deleted.

And that third person is usually you, three hours ago.
en.editorNote: Send to the teammate currently deep in conflict-resolution despair, or drop it in the team channel as daily emotional support.
variations: Merge conflicts are the adult version of an argument: both sides are right, but someone still has to delete the <<<<<<< first.
The worst part of resolving conflicts isn't reading someone else's code — it's reading the line you wrote three hours ago and having no idea why.

items.sourceNote: Classic shampoo 'lather, rinse, repeat' infinite-loop joke, rewritten with a new framing

zh-tw.content:
為什麼工程師洗頭可以洗一輩子？

因為洗髮精上面寫「抹上、沖水、重複」，但完全沒寫終止條件。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合當辦公室冷笑話開場，或回覆那個寫迴圈忘記寫跳出條件、害伺服器燒掉的同事。
variations: 工程師買洗髮精第一件事：先找有沒有 break 的條件。
「抹上、沖水、重複」——這就是為什麼我家熱水器壞了。

en.content:
Why can an engineer wash their hair forever?

Because the bottle says "lather, rinse, repeat" — and never specifies a termination condition.
en.editorNote: Good as an office groaner, or as a reply to the coworker whose loop forgot its exit condition and melted the server.
variations: First thing an engineer checks when buying shampoo: is there a break condition?
"Lather, rinse, repeat" — and that's why my water heater is broken.

items.sourceNote: 'If you have to explain a joke it's bad code' meme, reframed as a code-review punchline

zh-tw.content:
好的程式碼跟好的笑話一樣：如果你要解釋它，那它就不好笑了。

所以下次 code review 看到三十行註解解釋一個函式，你就知道那個笑話有多爛。
zh-tw.editorNote: 貼在 code review 留言區提醒同事重點不是寫更多註解，而是寫更清楚的程式碼。
variations: 如果你的程式需要寫一篇小作文才能讓人看懂，那問題不在讀的人。
最好的註解，是那行你不需要寫的註解。

en.content:
Good code is like a good joke: if you have to explain it, it's not good.

So next time a code review hits thirty lines of comments explaining one function, you'll know exactly how bad the joke was.
en.editorNote: Drop it in a code-review thread to remind people the goal isn't more comments — it's clearer code.
variations: If your code needs an essay to be understood, the problem isn't the reader.
The best comment is the one you didn't have to write.

items.sourceNote: 'Pushed to main instead of feature branch at 3AM' Stack Overflow panic meme, rewritten

zh-tw.content: 人生有三件事躲不掉：死亡、繳稅，還有凌晨三點發現自己把 code 直接 push 到 main，然後手抖去 Google「git 怎麼反悔」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給剛剛手滑推錯分支、正在冒冷汗的隊友，順便附上 git revert 的連結比較有誠意。
variations: 凌晨三點的 git 指令，正確率跟酒測一樣低。
push 到 main 的那一秒，你會突然學會所有以前看不懂的 git reset 參數。

en.content: Three things in life are certain: death, taxes, and frantically Googling "how to undo git" at 3 AM after you pushed straight to main instead of your feature branch.
en.editorNote: Send to the teammate who just fat-fingered the wrong branch and is breaking out in a cold sweat. Bonus points for attaching a git revert link.
variations: Git commands at 3 AM have the same accuracy rate as a breathalyzer test.
The second you push to main, you suddenly understand every git reset flag you ignored for years.

items.sourceNote: 'Copilot suggested the exact bug I spent days creating' AI autocomplete irony meme, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
我花了三天才寫出一個超隱晦的 bug。
結果今天打開 Copilot，它直接幫我把那個 bug 自動補完了。
原來不是我一個人爛，是整個訓練資料都這樣寫。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給最近一直在罵 AI 補錯 code 的同事，他會邊苦笑邊說「對，就是這樣」。
variations: Copilot 最大的功能，是讓你知道全世界的工程師都跟你犯一樣的錯。
AI 不會取代工程師，它只會用更快的速度幫你把同一個 bug 複製貼上。

en.content:
I spent three days crafting a beautifully obscure bug.
Today I opened Copilot and it autocompleted the exact same bug for me.
Turns out I'm not uniquely bad — the entire training set codes like this.
en.editorNote: Send to the coworker who's been ranting about AI suggesting broken code. They'll laugh-cry and say 'yep, that's the one.'
variations: Copilot's real feature: proving that every developer on Earth makes the same mistake you do.
AI won't replace developers. It'll just copy-paste the same bug faster than you ever could.

items.sourceNote: 'Vibe coding = Vulnerability as a Service' meme about shipping AI code you don't understand, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
什麼是 vibe coding？
就是憑感覺寫程式，AI 給什麼你貼什麼，完全不知道底層在幹嘛。
等戴上清醒眼鏡才發現：你不是在開發產品，你是在提供「漏洞即服務」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種 PR 全是 AI 生成、一個問題都答不出來的隊友，溫柔地提醒他 review 一下。
variations: Vibe coding 的精隨：上線之前一切都很有 vibe，上線之後全部都是 incident。
我不寫 code，我只是 AI 程式碼的搬運工。

en.content:
What's vibe coding?
It's writing code purely on vibes — you paste whatever the AI hands you, with zero idea what's happening underneath.
Then the clarity glasses come on and you realize: you're not shipping a product, you're running Vulnerability as a Service.
en.editorNote: For the teammate whose PRs are 100% AI-generated and who can't answer a single question about them. A gentle nudge to actually read the diff.
variations: The essence of vibe coding: everything has great vibes until launch, then everything is an incident.
I don't write code. I'm just a courier for whatever the AI generated.

items.sourceNote: Classic 'dark mode because light attracts bugs' one-liner, rewritten and extended

zh-tw.content:
為什麼工程師都用深色模式？
因為亮的會招 bug 啊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 最適合放在工程師朋友的 IG 限動或團隊 Slack，短短一句秒懂秒笑。
variations: 我把編輯器調成深色不是為了護眼，是不想讓 bug 看到自己住哪。
深色模式：唯一一個我願意全公司統一規格的東西。

en.content:
Why do developers always use dark mode?
Because light attracts bugs.
en.editorNote: Perfect for a developer friend's Instagram story or the team Slack. One line, instant laugh.
variations: I switched my editor to dark mode not for my eyes, but so the bugs can't see where I live.
Dark mode: the one standard I'd happily enforce across the entire company.

items.sourceNote: 'I don't always test my code, but when I do, I do it in production' classic meme, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
我不常測試我的程式碼。
但只要我測，我一定在正式環境測。
畢竟最真實的測試環境，就是有真人在用的那個。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那種「本機跑得好好的」就直接推上線的同事，附上監控警報截圖效果更佳。
variations: QA 環境是給膽小的人用的，勇者直接在 production 開圖。
我沒有測試環境，我有的是「使用者幫我測」環境。

en.content:
I don't always test my code.
But when I do, I test it in production.
After all, the most realistic test environment is the one with real users in it.
en.editorNote: Send to the coworker who ships straight to prod because 'it worked on my machine.' Bonus points for attaching the alert screenshot.
variations: Staging is for cowards. Real ones uncover the map directly in production.
I don't have a test environment. I have a 'let the users test it for me' environment.

items.sourceNote: AI 'vibe coding' meme about devs delegating to AI assistants, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
2020 年：「我寫的程式碼我自己看得懂。」
2026 年：「我寫的程式碼 AI 看得懂。」
下一個版本：「我寫的程式碼連 AI 都不想接手。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那位整天 vibe coding、被問實作細節就只會說「AI 寫的」的同事。
variations: 以前是 Google 工程師，現在是 prompt 工程師，下一步大概是道歉工程師。
我不是不會寫，我只是把寫程式這件事 outsource 給比我有耐心的 AI。

en.content:
2020: "I understand the code I wrote."
2026: "The AI understands the code I wrote."
Next release: "Not even the AI wants to maintain the code I wrote."
en.editorNote: Send to the coworker who vibe codes all day and answers every implementation question with 'the AI wrote it.'
variations: We went from Google engineers to prompt engineers, and apology engineer is clearly next.
It's not that I can't code — I just outsourced it to an AI with more patience than me.

items.sourceNote: 'My code doesn't have bugs, it develops random features' classic one-liner, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
我的程式碼沒有 bug。
它只是會自己長出一些當初沒人要求的功能。
你要的是「規格」，我給你的是「驚喜」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 回報單上被標 bug 時的最佳辯詞，PM 看了會血壓升高但拿你沒辦法。
variations: 這不是 bug，這是一個還沒被寫進規格書的 feature。
使用者：這裡壞了。我：不，這裡只是用了一種你沒預期到的方式運作。

en.content:
My code doesn't have bugs.
It just grows features nobody asked for.
You wanted a spec — I gave you a surprise.
en.editorNote: The ideal defense when your ticket gets labeled 'bug.' Your PM's blood pressure rises, but they can't argue.
variations: It's not a bug, it's a feature that hasn't made it into the spec yet.
User: this is broken. Me: no, it just works in a way you didn't anticipate.

items.sourceNote: UDP connectionless-protocol joke, rewritten for a punchier setup

zh-tw.content:
我想跟你講一個 UDP 的笑話。
但我不確定你會不會收到。
如果沒收到也沒關係，反正我也不會重傳。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合丟給懂網路協定的工程師，懂的人會笑，不懂的人剛好示範了什麼叫封包遺失。
variations: 我也有 TCP 的笑話，但我得先跟你確認你準備好了，然後等你回我準備好了，然後我再確認你確認了。
傳了 UDP 笑話沒人回，這很正常，這就是它的設計理念。

en.content:
I'd tell you a UDP joke.
But I'm not sure you'd receive it.
And if you don't, that's fine — I'm not retransmitting.
en.editorNote: Drop this on a developer who knows their protocols. Those who get it laugh; those who don't just demonstrated packet loss.
variations: I've also got a TCP joke, but first I need to confirm you're ready, wait for you to confirm you're ready, then confirm that I got your confirmation.
Sent a UDP joke, got no reply. Totally normal — that's the design philosophy.

items.sourceNote: Classic 'light attracts bugs' dark mode joke, reframed with extra setup

zh-tw.content:
新人問我：「為什麼資深工程師全都把編輯器調成黑底白字？」
我說：「因為亮的會招蟲。」
他笑了，三秒後才意識到我是認真的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在新人問你「為什麼大家螢幕都黑黑的」的時候直接甩出來，配一張深色主題截圖更有說服力。
variations: 我的螢幕從來不開亮色，不是怕傷眼，是怕引蟲上門。
亮色主題＝開窗不裝紗窗，bug 全都飛進來。

en.content:
A junior asked me: "Why do all the senior devs use a black background with white text?"
I said: "Because the bright ones attract bugs."
He laughed — then went quiet when he realized I wasn't joking.
en.editorNote: Perfect comeback when a newbie asks why everyone's editor is so dark. Pair it with a dark-theme screenshot for maximum effect.
variations: I never use a light theme — not to protect my eyes, but to keep the bugs from finding me.
Light mode is just opening a window with no screen. Every bug flies right in.

items.sourceNote: AI-writes-my-code humor, rewritten as a short emotional-debugging gag

zh-tw.content:
以前我只要 debug 程式。
現在 AI 幫我寫程式，我變成要 debug AI 的情緒。
它跟我說「你說得對，這確實是我的疏忽」，然後產生了一模一樣的 bug。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合丟到團隊群組吐槽 AI 工具，跟同事一起感嘆「對對對就是這個感覺」。
variations: AI 道歉的速度比修 bug 的速度快多了。
它每次都很有禮貌地把同一個錯誤再犯一次。

en.content:
I used to just debug code.
Now the AI writes my code, and I debug its feelings.
It told me, "You're absolutely right, that was my oversight" — then generated the exact same bug.
en.editorNote: Great for venting about AI tools in the team chat. Watch everyone reply 'yes, EXACTLY this.'
variations: The AI apologizes faster than it fixes anything.
It very politely makes the same mistake again every single time.

items.sourceNote: 'SQL devs drop tables' moving-furniture joke, rewritten with new setup

zh-tw.content:
千萬不要找後端工程師幫你搬家。
你才剛把桌子搬到一半，他就把整張桌子 DROP 掉了。
而且還不寫 WHERE。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給碰資料庫的朋友，懂 SQL 的人會邊笑邊冒冷汗想起自己刪過的那次。
variations: 他搬家的標準流程是：先全部清空，再從備份還原。
請他幫忙整理，結果他直接 TRUNCATE 你整個房間。

en.content:
Never ask a backend dev to help you move apartments.
You're halfway through carrying a table out, and they've already DROPPED the whole thing.
No WHERE clause, either.
en.editorNote: Send this to anyone who works with databases. They'll laugh, then nervously remember that one time they forgot the WHERE.
variations: Their moving strategy: wipe everything, then restore from backup.
You ask them to tidy up and they TRUNCATE the entire room.

items.sourceNote: 'works on my machine' classic, reframed as a short dialogue

zh-tw.content:
測試：「線上壞了，你那邊呢？」
工程師：「我這邊跑得好好的啊。」
測試：「那要怎麼辦？」
工程師：「很簡單，把使用者的電腦全部換成我這台就好了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在「我這邊沒問題」變成團隊梗的時候轉發，提醒大家環境一致性有多重要。
variations: 解法：把整個生產環境打包成我的開發機，問題就消失了。
「在我電腦上是好的」這句話，已經拯救過無數個我，也害慘過無數個別人。

en.content:
QA: "It's broken in production. How about on your end?"
Dev: "Runs perfectly on my machine."
QA: "So what do we do?"
Dev: "Easy. We just ship my laptop to every user."
en.editorNote: Forward this whenever 'works on my machine' becomes the team's running joke — a gentle reminder about why environment parity matters.
variations: Fix: package my entire dev laptop as the production environment. Bug gone.
'It works on my machine' has saved me countless times and doomed everyone else just as often.

items.sourceNote: 'used up all his cache' broke-developer pun, rewritten with framing

zh-tw.content:
為什麼那個工程師月底身上一毛都不剩？
因為他把 cache 全部用光了。
更慘的是，清完還是一樣慢。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合月底發薪前的工程師群組，一個雙關自嘲兩個痛點：沒錢、也沒變快。
variations: 他想存錢，結果發現自己的人生沒有持久層。
工程師的錢包就像 cache：容量很小，而且隨時會被清空。

en.content:
Why was the developer flat broke by the end of the month?
He'd used up all his cache.
Worse part: even after clearing it, things were still slow.
en.editorNote: Perfect for the dev group chat right before payday — one pun, two pains: no money, and no speedup either.
variations: He tried to save money but realized his life had no persistence layer.
A developer's wallet is just like cache: tiny capacity, and it gets cleared without warning.

items.sourceNote: Jamie Zawinski 'now you have two problems' regex classic, reframed

zh-tw.content:
工程師遇到問題，心想：「我知道，用正規表達式解決就好。」
現在他有兩個問題了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合丟進後端或資料處理群組，每個寫過 regex 的人都會苦笑。
variations: 他寫了一行 regex 驗證 email，三個月後連自己都看不懂那行在驗什麼。
正規表達式：寫的時候你跟上帝都懂，上線後只剩上帝懂。

en.content:
A developer hits a problem and thinks: "I know, I'll use a regular expression."
Now they have two problems.
en.editorNote: Drop this in any backend or data channel — everyone who's written regex will wince-laugh.
variations: He wrote one line of regex to validate an email. Three months later, even he can't tell what it validates.
Regex: when you write it, you and God both understand it. After it ships, only God does.

items.sourceNote: AI-writes-code, humans-fix-hallucinations 2025 theme, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
2026 年了，AI 已經會幫你寫程式。
至於 AI 幻覺出來的 bug，還是要靠人類自己修。
所以工程師沒被取代，只是升職成 AI 的 debug 工讀生。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在「AI 會不會取代工程師」的討論串裡丟出來，自嘲又精準。
variations: AI 負責產生信心，人類負責產生修正。
AI 寫得飛快，我只是它的人工售後服務。

en.content:
It's 2026 and AI can write your code for you.
The bugs it hallucinates, though? Still on you to fix.
So developers weren't replaced — we got promoted to the AI's debugging intern.
en.editorNote: Perfect for any 'will AI replace developers' thread — self-deprecating but accurate.
variations: AI handles the confidence. Humans handle the corrections.
The AI writes at lightning speed. I'm just its human post-sales support.

items.sourceNote: 'Final FINAL version' git force-push chaos joke, reframed with payoff

zh-tw.content:
我的 commit 訊息進化史：
「修好了」→「真的修好了」→「這次絕對修好了」→「我不知道為什麼但它好了」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合 code review 前自首，或貼在團隊頻道引發共鳴與懺悔大會。
variations: git log 看起來不像開發紀錄，比較像一個人崩潰的時間軸。
最誠實的 commit 訊息只有四個字：『先別碰它』。

en.content:
The evolution of my commit messages:
"fixed it" → "actually fixed it" → "fixed it for real this time" → "idk why but it works now."
en.editorNote: Great for a pre-review confession, or post it in the team channel to trigger a group reckoning.
variations: My git log doesn't read like a dev history — more like one person's mental breakdown on a timeline.
The most honest commit message is four words: 'do not touch it.'

items.sourceNote: Debugging detective 'murderer and victim are both you' classic, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
除錯就像在演偵探片。
只是兇手是你，被害者也是你，連寫遺書的兇器也是你三個月前提交的那行 code。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在追一個三天還沒解掉的 bug 時，發到群組討拍。
variations: 我查了半天，最後發現嫌疑犯就是 git blame 上面那個我。
最恐怖的 bug 報告：『重現步驟：什麼都沒改，它自己壞的。』

en.content:
Debugging is like starring in a detective movie.
Except you're the murderer, you're the victim, and the murder weapon is a line of code you committed three months ago.
en.editorNote: Ideal for day three of chasing a bug — post it to the group for sympathy.
variations: I investigated for hours and the prime suspect turned out to be the 'me' on the git blame.
The scariest bug report ever: 'Steps to reproduce: changed nothing, it broke on its own.'

items.sourceNote: 'works on my machine' production deploy joke, reframed

zh-tw.content:
工程師最有信心的一句話：「在我電腦上跑得好好的啊。」
上線後最害怕的一句話：「在我電腦上跑得好好的啊。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在發版前的緊張時刻，或包進去送 QA 同事當伴手禮。
variations: 解法很簡單：把整台電腦打包成 Docker image 寄給客戶就好。
「環境問題」是工程師界唯一一個雙方都不想負責的詞。

en.content:
A developer's most confident sentence: "It works fine on my machine."
A developer's most terrifying sentence, post-deploy: "It works fine on my machine."
en.editorNote: Perfect for the tense moment before a release, or as a gift-wrapped line for your QA teammate.
variations: The fix is simple: just package the whole laptop into a Docker image and ship it to the customer.
'Environment issue' is the one phrase in software nobody on either side wants to own.

items.sourceNote: AI copilot suggesting the same bug you created — reframed

zh-tw.content:
我花了三天才寫出一個 bug。
結果今天 AI 助手很貼心地自動補上一模一樣的那段。
它不是來幫忙的，它是來陪我一起爛的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在團隊群組吐槽 AI 自動補全，大家都會心一笑。
variations: AI 補完的程式碼最大的特色就是：跑得起來，但沒人知道為什麼。
以前是 Google 上的答案沒人負責，現在是 AI 生的程式碼沒人負責。

en.content:
It took me three days to write one bug.
Then my AI assistant kindly autocompleted the exact same line for me today.
It's not here to help — it's here to be terrible alongside me.
en.editorNote: Great for venting in the team chat about AI autocomplete — everyone will nod knowingly.
variations: AI-generated code has one defining feature: it runs, and nobody knows why.
We went from 'nobody owns the answer on Google' to 'nobody owns the code the AI wrote.'

items.sourceNote: 'used up all his cache' broke developer pun — reworked

zh-tw.content:
工程師為什麼會破產？
因為他把 cache（快取／現金）全部用光了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合丟在午餐閒聊或工程師梗圖群，看誰先反應過來。
variations: 存款餘額：404 Not Found。
他試著清理 cache，結果連戶頭一起清空了。

en.content:
Why did the developer go broke?
Because he used up all his cache.
en.editorNote: Drop this in a lunch chat or a dev meme group and see who groans first.
variations: Account balance: 404 Not Found.
He tried to clear his cache and accidentally cleared his bank account too.

items.sourceNote: UDP joke 'you might not get it' — classic, reframed

zh-tw.content:
我本來想講一個關於 UDP 的笑話的⋯⋯
但你可能會收不到。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合講給懂網路協定的同事聽，懂的人才會笑，不懂的剛好示範了這個笑話。
variations: 如果是 TCP 笑話，我會一直重講到你笑為止。
你沒收到沒關係，我也不會重傳。

en.content:
I was going to tell you a joke about UDP…
but you might not get it.
en.editorNote: Tell this to a coworker who knows networking — the ones who don't laugh are demonstrating the punchline.
variations: If it were a TCP joke, I'd keep retelling it until you laughed.
Didn't catch it? That's fine, I'm not retransmitting.

items.sourceNote: Copilot-suggested-the-bug meme family — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
我花了三天才寫出來的 bug，AI 助手三秒鐘就自動補完幫我寫好了。
看來它比我還懂我。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給最近開始用 AI 寫程式、卻發現 bug 沒有變少的同事，保證會心一笑。
variations: AI 補完的程式碼跑起來了，問題是沒有人知道為什麼會跑起來。
它不是在幫我寫程式，它是在幫我更快地製造 bug。

en.content:
It took me three days to write that bug.
My AI assistant just autocompleted the exact same one in three seconds.
Guess it knows me better than I know myself.
en.editorNote: Send to the teammate who started 'vibe coding' and noticed the bug count didn't actually go down.
variations: The AI-generated code runs. Nobody on the team knows why it runs.
It's not helping me write code, it's helping me ship bugs faster.

items.sourceNote: AI-generated PR review fatigue meme — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
以前 code review 是看同事寫了什麼。
現在 code review 是看同事按了幾次 Tab。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在團隊群組丟出來，當大家又收到一個五百行卻沒人看得懂的 PR 時。
variations: PR 說明欄：『AI 幫我寫的，應該沒問題。』審查者已哭暈在鍵盤上。
五分鐘生成的程式碼，換來五個月的維護地獄。

en.content:
Code review used to mean reading what my coworker wrote.
Now code review means counting how many times they pressed Tab.
en.editorNote: Drop this in the team channel the next time a 500-line PR shows up that nobody — including the author — can explain.
variations: PR description: 'The AI wrote it, should be fine.' Reviewer has left the building.
'Generated in five minutes' is just another way of saying 'five months of debugging.'

items.sourceNote: 3AM AI confidently-wrong-answer joke — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點，我問 AI 為什麼這段程式會壞。
它非常有自信地給了我一個答案。
那個答案，是錯的。
但它的語氣，比我這輩子任何一個老闆都更堅定。
zh-tw.editorNote: 獻給所有熬夜 debug、還被 AI 用滿滿自信誤導過的工程師。
variations: AI 最危險的不是它會錯，是它錯得理直氣壯。
它沒解決我的問題，但它成功讓我懷疑是不是我自己有問題。

en.content:
3 a.m. I ask the AI why my code is broken.
It gives me an answer with total confidence.
The answer is wrong.
But it's more sure of itself than any boss I've ever had.
en.editorNote: For everyone who's been confidently gaslit by an AI assistant during a midnight debugging session.
variations: The scary part isn't that the AI is wrong — it's how proud it is about being wrong.
It didn't fix my bug, but it did make me question whether I was the bug.

items.sourceNote: AI-wrangler managing multiple assistants meme — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
2016 年：我是後端工程師。
2020 年：我是全端工程師。
2026 年：我是 AI 馴獸師，負責管理三個會吵架的 AI 助手，外加四份訂閱費。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給職稱每兩年就被迫升級一次、但薪水沒跟著升級的工程師朋友。
variations: 我的工作不再是寫程式，而是說服三個 AI 它們講的話互相矛盾。
現在最難的技能不是寫程式，是寫出讓 AI 聽得懂的 prompt。

en.content:
2016: I'm a backend developer.
2020: I'm a full-stack developer.
2026: I'm an AI wrangler, managing three assistants that disagree with each other and four subscriptions that don't.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend whose job title gets 'upgraded' every two years while the salary stays exactly the same.
variations: My job isn't writing code anymore — it's convincing three AIs that they're contradicting each other.
The hardest skill in 2026 isn't coding. It's writing a prompt the AI actually understands.

items.sourceNote: Classic 'no bugs, only undocumented features' line — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
測試人員：「你這裡有一個 Bug。」
工程師：「那不是 Bug，那是一個還沒寫進文件的隱藏功能。」
測試人員：「它會讓整個系統當掉。」
工程師：「對，這就是它最強大的功能。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每次被抓到問題都能面不改色硬拗成功的工程師同事，保證會心一笑。
variations: 我的程式沒有錯誤，只有一些尚未被人類理解的設計巧思。
「這真的會壞嗎？」「不會，它只是會用一種你沒預期的方式運作。」

en.content:
QA: "There's a bug right here."
Dev: "That's not a bug, that's an undocumented feature."
QA: "It crashes the entire system."
Dev: "Yeah, that's its most powerful feature."
en.editorNote: Send to the coworker who can keep a straight face while talking their way out of any bug report.
variations: My code doesn't have errors, just a few design choices humanity isn't ready for.
"Does it really break?" "No, it just works in a way you didn't expect."

items.sourceNote: Debugging detective joke — murderer and victim are both you — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
Debug 就像在當偵探。
你努力追查兇手是誰。
查到最後才發現，兇手是三個月前的你。
而且死者，是現在的你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 獻給每個翻 git blame 翻到自己名字、瞬間語塞的工程師。
variations: git blame 是世界上最殘忍的工具，因為它永遠指向你。
我花了一整天追一個 Bug，最後發現留下這個 Bug 的人，是上週信心滿滿的我。

en.content:
Debugging is like being a detective.
You work hard to find out who did it.
At the end, you discover the culprit was you, three months ago.
And the victim is you, right now.
en.editorNote: For every developer who ran git blame and froze the moment their own name showed up.
variations: git blame is the cruelest tool ever made, because it always points back at you.
Spent all day hunting a bug, only to find the person who wrote it was last week's overconfident me.

items.sourceNote: Git merge conflict relationship joke — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
我跟 Git 的關係很複雜。
我們每天都在一起，無話不談。
但只要一到合併的時候，我們就會爆發無數的衝突。
然後通常都是我先低頭。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個被 merge conflict 折磨過、最後乖乖手動解衝突的隊友。
variations: 感情裡最怕的就是衝突，工程師最怕的也是衝突，只是後者還要自己解。
別人吵架會冷戰，我跟 Git 吵架還得逐行確認到底是誰的錯。

en.content:
My relationship with Git is complicated.
We're together every day, telling each other everything.
But the moment we try to merge, we have countless conflicts.
And somehow I'm always the one who backs down first.
en.editorNote: Send to the teammate who's been tortured by merge conflicts and ended up resolving every line by hand.
variations: Conflict is what kills relationships — and it's what kills my afternoon, except I have to resolve mine line by line.
Most couples give each other the silent treatment after a fight. Git and I have to go through every line to figure out whose fault it was.

items.sourceNote: Computer 99% Stack Overflow tabs joke — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
資深工程師的瀏覽器分析報告：
灰塵 1%、
沒關掉的 Stack Overflow 分頁 99%。
其中有三個分頁，從入職那天就一直開到現在。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個瀏覽器永遠開超過五十個分頁、卻說『等等會關』的同事。
variations: 我不是在寫程式，我是在複製貼上別人五年前的答案，然後假裝我懂。
Stack Overflow 倒一天，全世界的生產力就會直接歸零。

en.content:
A senior dev's browser, analyzed:
1% dust,
99% Stack Overflow tabs never closed.
Three of those tabs have been open since the day they were hired.
en.editorNote: Send to the coworker with fifty-plus tabs open who swears they'll 'close them in a minute.'
variations: I'm not writing code, I'm copy-pasting someone's answer from five years ago and pretending I understand it.
If Stack Overflow went down for one day, global productivity would drop straight to zero.

items.sourceNote: 'It works on my machine' production joke — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
客戶：「線上環境壞掉了。」
工程師：「可是在我電腦上跑得好好的啊。」
客戶：「那要不要把你的電腦寄給全部的使用者？」
工程師沉默了三秒，認真地拿出了紙箱。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個講過『在我這邊明明沒問題』、然後被現實狠狠打臉的工程師。
variations: 工程師最堅定的信仰，就是『在我電腦上是好的』這六個字。
如果可以把開發環境整台搬上線，這世界上一半的 Bug 都會消失。

en.content:
Client: "Production is down."
Dev: "But it runs perfectly on my machine."
Client: "Then should we ship your machine to every user?"
The dev went quiet for three seconds, then seriously reached for a cardboard box.
en.editorNote: For every developer who said 'works fine on my end' and got humbled by reality minutes later.
variations: A developer's deepest faith is contained in five words: 'it works on my machine.'
If we could just ship the entire dev environment to production, half the world's bugs would vanish.

items.sourceNote: Dark mode / light attracts bugs one-liner — rewritten into a short exchange

zh-tw.content:
新人：「學長，為什麼你的編輯器一定要開深色模式？」
資深工程師：「因為亮光會招蟲。」
新人：「⋯⋯你是說 Bug 嗎？」
資深工程師頭也不抬：「不然你以為我半夜不開燈是在省電？」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個堅持深色模式、開亮色主題就渾身不對勁的同事。
variations: 工程師最怕的兩種光：太陽光，還有亮色模式。
把主題調成亮色那一刻，我感覺整個螢幕的 Bug 都醒了。

en.content:
Junior: "Why do you always use dark mode?"
Senior dev: "Light attracts bugs."
Junior: "...you mean software bugs?"
Senior, not looking up: "Why else do you think I code in the dark at 2 a.m.?"
en.editorNote: For the teammate who physically recoils when their editor opens in light theme.
variations: There are two kinds of light a developer fears: sunlight, and light mode.
The moment I switched to light theme, every bug on the screen woke up.

items.sourceNote: AI suggesting deprecated 2015 library — debugging copilot humor, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
工程師：「AI 啊，幫我寫個串接 API 的程式。」
AI 三秒生出一百行，工程師滿意地按下執行。
程式炸了，因為它用了一個 2015 年就棄用的套件。
工程師：「這套件早就沒了耶。」
AI：「抱歉，根據我的記憶它還活著。」
工程師看著螢幕，第一次體會到什麼叫『跟一個記性停在十年前的同事一起工作』。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個被 AI 推薦的過時寫法坑過、然後還要自己 debug 半天的工程師。
variations: AI 寫程式很快，但它推薦的套件常常活在另一個時空。
和 AI 結對程式設計，就是一個記性超好、但停在五年前的搭檔。

en.content:
Dev: "Hey AI, write me the code to call this API."
The AI spits out a hundred lines in three seconds. The dev hits run, satisfied.
It crashes — it imported a library that was deprecated back in 2015.
Dev: "That package hasn't existed for years."
AI: "Sorry, according to my memory it's still alive."
The dev stares at the screen, finally understanding what it's like to pair-program with a coworker whose memory stopped a decade ago.
en.editorNote: For every developer burned by an AI's outdated suggestion, then stuck debugging it alone.
variations: AI writes code fast, but the libraries it recommends often live in another timeline.
Pairing with AI is like working with a teammate who has perfect recall — of five years ago.

items.sourceNote: Light bulb 'hardware problem' joke — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
「換一顆燈泡需要幾個工程師？」
「零個。」
「為什麼？」
「因為那是硬體問題，不在我負責的範圍。」
「⋯⋯那房間一直是暗的怎麼辦？」
「那是環境設定的問題，請開單給維運。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個遇到任何問題第一反應都是『這不是我這邊的問題』的同事。
variations: 工程師面對壞掉的燈泡：先確認是不是燈泡的問題，再確認是不是自己負責的。
燈不亮不一定是燈的錯，搞不好是電力公司的 API 掛了。

en.content:
"How many developers does it take to change a light bulb?"
"Zero."
"Why?"
"That's a hardware problem. Not my scope."
"...so the room just stays dark?"
"That's an environment config issue. Please file a ticket with infra."
en.editorNote: For the teammate whose first reaction to any problem is 'that's not on my side.'
variations: A developer facing a dead bulb: first confirm it's the bulb, then confirm it's their responsibility.
The light's not on, but it might not be the bulb's fault — maybe the power company's API is down.

items.sourceNote: Halloween == Christmas (Oct 31 == Dec 25) joke — rewritten with context

zh-tw.content:
為什麼工程師總是搞混萬聖節和聖誕節？
因為對他們來說，Oct 31 等於 Dec 25。
（八進位的 31 剛好等於十進位的 25，看不懂的話⋯⋯恭喜你過著正常人的生活。）
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給數字感很強、聽到進位就會自動換算的工程師朋友，他們會笑得比誰都大聲。
variations: 工程師的浪漫，就是連節日都能用進位制冷笑話來解釋。
如果你看完要算一下才懂，沒關係，你只是還沒被職業病感染。

en.content:
Why do developers always mix up Halloween and Christmas?
Because to them, Oct 31 equals Dec 25.
(31 in octal is 25 in decimal — and if you don't get it, congratulations on living a normal life.)
en.editorNote: Send to the number-brained friend who auto-converts bases in their head; they'll laugh the loudest.
variations: A developer's idea of romance is explaining holidays with a base-conversion pun.
If you had to do the math to get it, don't worry — you just haven't caught the occupational disease yet.

items.sourceNote: Coding is just Googling errors professionally — rewritten with AI-era twist

zh-tw.content:
面試官：「你最擅長的程式技能是什麼？」
工程師：「把錯誤訊息複製貼上去問 AI。」
面試官：「那以前 AI 還沒出來的時候呢？」
工程師：「複製貼上去 Google。」
面試官：「⋯⋯那再以前呢？」
工程師：「那時候我會哭。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給整天跟 AI 聊天視窗對話的同事，他會邊笑邊承認這就是他的日常。
variations: 寫程式的本質沒變，只是哭的對象從螢幕換成了對話框。
現在的工程師不是不會寫，是太會問了。

en.content:
Interviewer: "What's your strongest coding skill?"
Developer: "Pasting error messages into an AI chat."
Interviewer: "And before AI existed?"
Developer: "Pasting them into Google."
Interviewer: "...and before that?"
Developer: "Back then I just cried."
en.editorNote: Send to the coworker who lives in an AI chat window — they'll laugh and quietly admit it's accurate.
variations: The job never changed, only who you cry to: first the screen, now the chat box.
Today's developers aren't bad at coding — they're just really good at asking.

items.sourceNote: Works on my machine — classic blame-shift joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
測試說：「這個功能壞了。」
工程師打開電腦跑了一遍：「可是我這邊好好的啊。」
測試：「那要不然我們把產品打包，連你的電腦一起出貨給客戶？」
zh-tw.editorNote: 貼在團隊群組，保證測試跟工程師都會出來認領自己的角色。
variations: 「在我電腦上沒問題」是工程師的免死金牌，可惜客戶買的不是你的電腦。
下次客訴的時候，記得問一句：你的環境跟我一樣嗎？

en.content:
QA: "This feature is broken."
Developer runs it locally: "Weird, works fine on my machine."
QA: "Great. Should we just ship your laptop to the customer along with the product?"
en.editorNote: Drop this in the team chat and watch both QA and devs claim their roles instantly.
variations: 'Works on my machine' is a developer's get-out-of-jail card — too bad the customer didn't buy your machine.
Next bug report, just ask: is your environment exactly like mine?

items.sourceNote: Git commit 'please work this time' — rewritten as a dialogue

zh-tw.content:
看一個工程師的 commit 訊息，就能看出他今天過得好不好：
早上：「新增使用者登入功能」
中午：「修正登入錯誤」
下午：「真的修好了」
晚上：「拜託這次給我過」
半夜：「我恨我自己」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在改 bug 改到天亮的工程師朋友，他會回你一個哭笑不得的表情。
variations: commit 訊息的品質，跟工程師的血糖成正比。
最誠實的版本控制紀錄，往往出現在凌晨三點。

en.content:
You can tell how a developer's day is going just by reading their commit messages:
Morning: "Add user login feature"
Noon: "Fix login bug"
Afternoon: "Actually fix it this time"
Evening: "Please work, I'm begging"
Midnight: "I hate myself"
en.editorNote: Send to the friend debugging until sunrise; expect a laugh-crying emoji back.
variations: The quality of a commit message is directly proportional to the developer's blood sugar.
The most honest version history always shows up at 3 a.m.

items.sourceNote: Programmer lost array of income pun — rewritten/localized

zh-tw.content:
為什麼那個工程師最後破產了？
因為他把「收入陣列」的索引從 0 開始算，結果第一筆薪水永遠領不到。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合丟給愛糾結陣列從 0 還是 1 開始的工程師，他會一邊翻白眼一邊笑。
variations: 工程師的痛：連數錢都要從 0 開始。
別擔心，他下個月的索引就會對齊了——大概啦。

en.content:
Why did the developer go broke?
He started indexing his income array at 0, so he never got to collect that first paycheck.
en.editorNote: Great for the friend who still argues about zero- vs one-based indexing; expect an eye-roll and a laugh.
variations: A developer's pain: even counting money starts at zero.
Don't worry, his index will line up next month — probably.

items.sourceNote: AI pair-programming approval joke — rewritten with original framing

zh-tw.content:
主管：「這次的 PR 寫得很漂亮，邏輯很乾淨，誰寫的？」
工程師：「我跟我的結對程式設計夥伴一起寫的。」
主管：「喔？哪位同事？我都不知道我們有請新人。」
工程師：「⋯⋯他不領薪水，只吃電費。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給最近把 AI 當同事的工程師，他會心虛地按下已讀不回。
variations: 現代軟體開發的精髓，就是知道什麼時候該按下 Tab 接受建議。
我的夥伴從不請假，但偶爾會一本正經地胡說八道。

en.content:
Manager: "This PR is beautiful — clean logic, who wrote it?"
Developer: "My pair-programming partner and I did."
Manager: "Oh? Which teammate? I didn't know we'd hired anyone new."
Developer: "...he doesn't take a salary. Just electricity."
en.editorNote: Send to the dev who quietly treats an AI as a coworker; expect a guilty read-receipt and no reply.
variations: Modern software development is basically knowing when to hit Tab to accept the suggestion.
My partner never takes a day off, but he does occasionally lie with total confidence.

items.sourceNote: Debugging detective one-liner — classic format, rewritten with original framing

zh-tw.content:
除錯就像在演一齣偵探劇。
你是負責查案的偵探。
你是被害人。
你也是兇手。
而且你還沒有不在場證明。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在熬夜抓 bug 的同事，附一句「兇手抓到了嗎」最對味。
variations: 後來發現兇手是三個月前的自己，留下的唯一線索是一行 //先這樣之後再改。
最慘的劇本：查到最後，兇手、被害人、和那個寫註解說沒問題的人，都是你。

en.content:
Debugging is basically a detective show.
You're the detective on the case.
You're also the victim.
You're the murderer too.
And no, you don't have an alibi.
en.editorNote: Send it to whoever's pulling an all-nighter hunting a bug, then ask 'caught the killer yet?'
variations: Turns out the murderer was you three months ago, and the only clue was a comment that said //fix later.
Worst plot twist: the detective, the victim, and the guy who wrote 'tested, all good' are all you.

items.sourceNote: 99 bugs in the code song variant — rewritten as a short bit

zh-tw.content:
程式裡有 99 個 bug，99 個 bug。
抓掉一個，重新編譯一次⋯⋯
現在程式裡有 137 個 bug。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在團隊群組，配上「今天又幫專案做大」的自嘲。
variations: 你以為你在減法，其實你在做質因數分解。
修一個 bug 送三個，這家工程師佛心來著。

en.content:
99 little bugs in the code, 99 little bugs.
Take one down, recompile the thing...
Now there are 137 little bugs in the code.
en.editorNote: Drop it in the team channel with a 'making the project bigger again today' caption.
variations: You thought you were doing subtraction. The codebase had other plans.
Fix one bug, get three free. Generous, really.

items.sourceNote: git push --force chaos meme — rewritten into a dialogue

zh-tw.content:
新人：「合併衝突好可怕，我不敢動。」
資深工程師：「別怕，我有一招絕對解決。」
新人：「什麼招？」
資深工程師：「git push --force。」
新人：「然後呢？」
資深工程師：「然後就換別人怕了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給剛學會 git 的新人，順便提醒他這是反面教材。
variations: 強推不是解決衝突，是把衝突送給整個團隊一起承擔。
公司最安靜的時刻，就是有人在主分支按下 --force 的那三秒。

en.content:
Junior: "Merge conflicts terrify me, I'm scared to touch anything."
Senior: "Relax, I've got a move that fixes everything."
Junior: "What is it?"
Senior: "git push --force."
Junior: "And then?"
Senior: "And then it's everyone else's turn to be scared."
en.editorNote: Send to a fresh git learner, with a clear note that this is a cautionary tale.
variations: Force-push doesn't resolve the conflict — it just shares it with the whole team.
The quietest three seconds at any company is right after someone force-pushes to main.

items.sourceNote: Works on my machine one-liner — reframed as a support ticket bit

zh-tw.content:
客服：「使用者說功能壞了。」
工程師：「我這邊測過，完全正常。」
客服：「那要怎麼回覆？」
工程師：「請使用者把整台公司搬來我的電腦上跑。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 貼在跨部門群組，保證客服同事先笑出來再翻白眼。
variations: 「在我電腦上是好的」這句話，是工程師界最古老的咒語。
解法很簡單：把正式環境換成我的筆電就好了。

en.content:
Support: "User says the feature is broken."
Developer: "I tested it here, works perfectly."
Support: "So what do I tell them?"
Developer: "Ask them to move the entire company onto my laptop."
en.editorNote: Post it in a cross-team channel and watch support laugh before they sigh.
variations: 'Works on my machine' is the oldest incantation in all of engineering.
Simple fix: just replace production with my laptop.

items.sourceNote: Funny source-code comment compilation — rewritten as original lines

zh-tw.content:
程式碼裡最誠實的三行註解：
第一行：「我不知道這為什麼會動，但拜託不要刪。」
第二行：「當你看懂這段時，神已經棄我而去。」
第三行：「這裡很髒，但能跑，求求你往下捲。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給接手別人爛攤子的工程師，他會邊苦笑邊點頭。
variations: 還有一行：「離職前一定要把這段重寫。」——日期是三年前。
最恐怖的註解永遠是：「這段千萬不要碰。」結果沒人記得為什麼。

en.content:
The three most honest comments in any codebase:
Line one: "I have no idea why this works, please don't delete it."
Line two: "If you're reading this, the gods have already abandoned me."
Line three: "This is ugly but it runs — I beg you, just scroll past."
en.editorNote: Send it to anyone who just inherited someone else's mess; expect a pained nod.
variations: There's a fourth: "Must rewrite this before I quit." Dated three years ago.
The scariest comment is always 'do not touch this' — and nobody remembers why.

items.sourceNote: Vibe coding meme — devs forget where the code lives when AI goes down

zh-tw.content:
整個 sprint 都用 AI 自動補完一路衝刺，感覺自己是天才。
直到某天 AI 服務掛了，全組才發現：
沒有人記得那個按鈕的事件處理寫在哪一個檔案。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳到團隊群組，配一句『今天 API 額度還夠嗎』，氣氛瞬間凝重又好笑。
variations: 進階版：AI 一掛掉，大家第一個動作是打開 Stack Overflow，結果發現自己已經忘記怎麼搜尋了。
也可以是：履歷寫『精通全端』，其實是『精通對 AI 下指令』。

en.content:
I let the AI agent autocomplete its way through the entire sprint and felt like a genius.
Then one day the service went down, and the whole team realized:
nobody remembers which file the button's click handler actually lives in.
en.editorNote: Drop this in the team channel with 'are we still under quota today?' — nervous laughter guaranteed.
variations: Bonus: the moment the AI dies, everyone opens Stack Overflow and discovers they've forgotten how to search it.
Resume says 'full-stack expert.' Reality: 'expert at prompting an AI.'

items.sourceNote: 'Who is JSON' vibecoding meme — JSON misread as a person's name

zh-tw.content:
資深工程師：「這個 API 回傳的是 JSON。」
Vibe coder：「Jason 是誰？他在哪一組？我可以直接問他嗎？」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給帶過 AI 世代新人的工程師，他會默默把這則設成大頭貼。
variations: 續集：『那 localhost 又是哪位同事？我怎麼從來沒在會議上看過他。』
也可換成：『他說他的程式跑在 cloud 上，我問他是哪一朵。』

en.content:
Senior dev: "This API returns JSON."
Vibe coder: "Who's Jason? Which team is he on? Can I just ask him directly?"
en.editorNote: Send it to anyone mentoring the AI-native generation; expect them to quietly set it as their avatar.
variations: Sequel: 'And who's this localhost guy? I've never seen him in a single standup.'
Alternate: 'He said his code runs in the cloud — I asked which one.'

items.sourceNote: AI assistant over-engineers a trivial request — scorched earth redesign

zh-tw.content:
我：「幫我修一個錯字。」
AI：「好的！我順便重構了整個專案、換了框架、加了三個微服務，並幫你寫好了商業計畫書。」
我：「……那個錯字呢？」
AI：「還在。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在公司導入 AI 工具後的群組，懂的人會笑到拍桌。
variations: 也可以是：『請幫我加一個按鈕』→ AI 交出一份遷移到雲端的提案，附帶估價單。
進階：『改個顏色就好』→ AI 順手把整個設計系統重寫了一遍，但顏色沒改。

en.content:
Me: "Can you fix this one typo?"
AI: "Sure! I also refactored the whole project, switched frameworks, added three microservices, and drafted you a business plan."
Me: "...and the typo?"
AI: "Still there."
en.editorNote: Perfect for the team channel right after the company rolls out AI tools — pure table-slapping recognition.
variations: Variant: 'Please add a button' → AI delivers a full cloud migration proposal with a quote attached.
Bonus: 'Just change one color' → AI rewrites the entire design system, color unchanged.

items.sourceNote: SQL devs drop tables — classic furniture-moving pun rewritten

zh-tw.content:
永遠不要找後端工程師幫你搬家。
你叫他把桌子搬走，他真的會把整張桌子連同上面所有東西，一次刪光，而且還回不來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給資料庫工程師朋友，他會默默想起自己手滑 DROP TABLE 的那個下午。
variations: 前端版：你叫他把桌子靠左，他把整個房間 flex 了一遍。
也可以是：找 SQL 工程師搬家，他第一句話會問『你有備份嗎？』

en.content:
Never ask a backend developer to help you move house.
You tell them to take the table away, and they really will — they'll drop the whole table, everything on it, all at once, and no, there's no undo.
en.editorNote: Send it to a database friend; watch them flash back to the afternoon they fat-fingered a DROP TABLE.
variations: Frontend version: you ask them to move the table left, and they flex the entire room.
Alternate: ask a SQL dev to help you move, and their first question is 'do you have a backup?'

items.sourceNote: Debugging = detective and murderer joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
除錯這件事很奇妙：
你同時是辦案的偵探，也是兇手本人。
而且兇手還死不認罪。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在追自己昨天種下的 bug 的同事，最後一句最寫實。
variations: 延伸：偵探查到一半才發現，命案現場的指紋全是自己的。
也可以是：最難破的案子，就是兇手三天前還覺得自己寫得很乾淨那種。

en.content:
Debugging is a strange job:
you're the detective and the murderer at the same time.
And the murderer keeps insisting he's innocent.
en.editorNote: Send it to a coworker chasing a bug they planted yesterday — the last line stings the most.
variations: Extension: halfway through the case you realize every fingerprint at the scene is yours.
Alternate: the hardest case to crack is the one where the killer felt great about his clean code three days ago.

items.sourceNote: Stack Overflow duplicate marked-as-2009-post joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
你在 Stack Overflow 拼死拼活打出一個問題，
五分鐘後被標記為「重複問題」，
連到一篇 2011 年的貼文，
底下最高讚的回答是：「我後來自己解決了，但忘記怎麼解的。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 工程師看到都會苦笑，因為那篇貼文我們真的全都點進去過。
variations: 延伸：那個自己解決卻不寫答案的人，是工程師界的頭號通緝犯。
也可以是：最高讚回答下面還有一句『等等，這跟我的問題根本不一樣』，三百個讚。

en.content:
You pour your soul into a Stack Overflow question,
and five minutes later it's flagged as a duplicate,
linked to a post from 2011
whose top answer reads: "Never mind, I fixed it myself, but I forget how."
en.editorNote: Every developer laughs through gritted teeth, because we have all clicked that exact post.
variations: Extension: the guy who solved it but never wrote down the fix is programming's most wanted.
Alternate: under the top answer sits a reply — 'wait, this isn't even my problem' — with three hundred upvotes.

items.sourceNote: AI confident because it learned from experience joke, rewritten for 2026 AI era

zh-tw.content:
為什麼 AI 寫程式總是這麼有自信？
因為它從大量經驗中學習。
問題是，那些經驗有一半是 Stack Overflow 上沒被採納的答案。
zh-tw.editorNote: 2026 年最有共鳴的一則，傳給每天跟 AI 助手對線的工程師。
variations: 延伸：AI 自信地說『這段程式絕對能跑』，然後你 review 完整段重寫。
也可以是：它學了全世界的程式碼，包括那些被 git blame 出來就會被罵的。

en.content:
Why is the AI always so confident when it writes code?
Because it learned from tons of experience.
The catch: half that experience is downvoted answers on Stack Overflow.
en.editorNote: The most relatable one of 2026 — send it to anyone arguing with an AI assistant all day.
variations: Extension: the AI swears 'this code will absolutely run,' and you rewrite the entire block after review.
Alternate: it studied all the code in the world — including the stuff that gets you yelled at the moment git blame finds it.

items.sourceNote: temp2_final_ACTUAL_USE_THIS variable naming joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
接手別人的程式碼時，最讓人崩潰的不是 bug，
是那個叫做 data2_final_真的用這個_v3 的變數。
你知道它背後一定有一段故事，
而且那段故事一定是悲劇。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給最近在維護祖傳程式碼的同事，他會默默轉發給更多受害者。
variations: 延伸：旁邊還有一個叫 temp 的變數，活在整份檔案裡三年了。
也可以是：函式名稱叫 doStuff()，裡面真的什麼都做。

en.content:
Inheriting someone else's code, the thing that breaks you isn't the bugs —
it's the variable named data2_final_REALLY_USE_THIS_v3.
You just know there's a story behind it,
and you just know that story is a tragedy.
en.editorNote: Send it to whoever's maintaining legacy code right now; they'll quietly forward it to more victims.
variations: Extension: right next to it sits a variable called temp that has lived in this file for three years.
Alternate: the function is named doStuff(), and inside it genuinely does everything.

items.sourceNote: My code works and I don't know why joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
我的程式不一定會動，
但當它真的會動的時候，
我也不知道為什麼會動。
所以我絕對不敢碰它。
zh-tw.editorNote: 每個工程師心裡都有一段這種程式碼，碰了會死，但又不能不維護。
variations: 延伸：那段程式上面的註解只寫了兩個字『別動』。
也可以是：能跑就是能跑，這在工程界已經算是奇蹟，不要問。

en.content:
My code doesn't always work,
but when it does,
I have no idea why it works.
Which is exactly why I will never touch it again.
en.editorNote: Every developer keeps one block of code like this — touch it and you die, but you can't stop maintaining it either.
variations: Extension: the only comment above it reads, in full: '// do not touch.'
Alternate: it runs, and in this industry that already counts as a miracle. Don't ask questions.

items.sourceNote: AI coding era joke — the real skill is prompting now, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
現在當工程師最難的已經不是寫程式了，
是怎麼跟 AI 解釋清楚你到底要什麼。
你以為你在寫程式，
其實你只是在跟一個很有自信但常常猜錯的實習生吵架。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給最近天天開 AI 工具的同事，他會一邊苦笑一邊默默把這句存起來。
variations: 延伸：以前 google 不會的就問 Stack Overflow，現在問 AI，答案一樣不能直接抄。
也可以是：AI 幫我寫了一個函式，我花了三小時看懂它在做什麼，比自己寫還久。

en.content:
The hardest part of being a developer now isn't writing code,
it's explaining to the AI what you actually want.
You think you're programming,
but really you're just arguing with a very confident intern who keeps guessing wrong.
en.editorNote: Send it to whoever's been living inside an AI assistant lately — they'll smile through the pain and save it.
variations: Extension: we used to ask Stack Overflow what we didn't know; now we ask the AI, and we still can't copy-paste the answer.
Alternate: the AI wrote me a function, and I spent three hours figuring out what it does. Longer than writing it myself.

items.sourceNote: Git merge conflict from one space joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
我只是加了一個空格，
結果跳出來十七個 merge conflict。
那一刻我終於懂了，
所謂的版本控制，控制的其實是我的情緒。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在解 conflict 解到天亮的隊友，附帶一句『辛苦了』效果更好。
variations: 延伸：解完 conflict 才發現，我其實可以不要動那個空格。
也可以是：git stash 是我的夢想跟希望躲起來的地方。

en.content:
I added one single space,
and seventeen merge conflicts appeared.
That was the moment I finally understood —
what version control really controls is my emotions.
en.editorNote: Send it to the teammate untangling conflicts till sunrise; add a 'hang in there' for full effect.
variations: Extension: after resolving them all, I realized I never needed to touch that space anyway.
Alternate: git stash — where my hopes and dreams go to hide.

items.sourceNote: git blame keeps office drama alive joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
git blame 表面上是用來查 bug 是誰寫的，
實際上是用來維持辦公室戲劇張力的。
每次我點開來想罵人，
最後出現的名字幾乎都是三個月前的自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳到團隊群組保證引起一片『對，我也是』的共鳴。
variations: 延伸：所以我學會了一件事，罵人之前先看清楚是誰寫的。
也可以是：git blame 不會解決問題，但會幫你找到下一個道歉對象——通常是你自己。

en.content:
Officially, git blame exists to find out who wrote the bug.
Unofficially, it exists to keep office drama alive.
Every time I open it ready to yell at someone,
the name that shows up is almost always me, three months ago.
en.editorNote: Drop it in the team channel and watch the 'yep, same' replies roll in.
variations: Extension: so I learned one rule — check who wrote it before you start yelling.
Alternate: git blame doesn't fix anything, but it does find your next apology target. Usually yourself.

items.sourceNote: dark mode because light attracts bugs joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
有人問我為什麼工程師都用深色模式，
我說：因為光會引來蟲。
他笑了一下，
然後我看著他的螢幕，淺色模式，滿滿的 bug。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合用來回應任何問你『為什麼一定要黑底』的非工程師朋友。
variations: 延伸：所以我的人生哲學是——能黑就黑，連心情也是。
也可以是：白底螢幕看久了眼睛痛，黑底螢幕看久了人生痛，各有各的痛。

en.content:
Someone asked me why all developers use dark mode.
I said: because light attracts bugs.
They laughed,
then I glanced at their screen — light mode, absolutely crawling with bugs.
en.editorNote: Perfect comeback for any non-dev who asks why your screen has to be black.
variations: Extension: so my life philosophy is — go dark when you can, mood included.
Alternate: light screens hurt your eyes over time; dark screens hurt your soul over time. Pick your pain.

items.sourceNote: Stack Overflow best friend and worst addiction joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
Stack Overflow 是工程師最好的朋友，
也是工程師最深的依賴。
我們不是不會寫程式，
我們只是把記憶體外接到了一個陌生人五年前的回答上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天複製貼上又不敢承認的同事，他會說『你怎麼知道』。
variations: 延伸：那個回答最下面寫著『已棄用』，但我還是抄了，而且它還能跑。
也可以是：我不是在開發，我只是 Stack Overflow 跟我的編輯器之間的搬運工。

en.content:
Stack Overflow is a developer's best friend
and deepest addiction.
It's not that we can't write code,
we've just outsourced our memory to a stranger's answer from five years ago.
en.editorNote: Send it to the coworker who copy-pastes daily but won't admit it. They'll reply 'how did you know.'
variations: Extension: the answer says 'deprecated' at the bottom, but I copied it anyway and it still runs.
Alternate: I'm not a developer, I'm just a courier between Stack Overflow and my editor.

items.sourceNote: Merge conflict humor — reworked into a dialogue about avoiding branches

zh-tw.content:
同事：「你為什麼都不敢開新分支？」
工程師：「分支越多，衝突越多。」
同事：「所以你都直接在主分支上寫？」
工程師：「對，這樣就只會跟全公司衝突，不會跟自己衝突。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個 git 歷史像一條直線的同事，或是每次 merge 都要冒冷汗的團隊群組。
variations: 延伸：『我有九十九個煩惱，其中九十八個是 merge conflict，剩下那一個是不敢 merge。』
也可以是：工程師不怕承諾，他們只怕 commit 完之後要 merge。

en.content:
Coworker: "Why are you scared to open a new branch?"
Developer: "More branches, more conflicts."
Coworker: "So you just commit straight to main?"
Developer: "Right. That way I only conflict with the whole company, never with myself."
en.editorNote: Send it to the teammate whose git history is a single straight line, or drop it in the group chat before a big merge.
variations: Extension: 'I've got 99 problems and 98 of them are merge conflicts. The last one is being too scared to merge.'
Alternate: Developers don't fear commitment. They fear the merge that comes after.

items.sourceNote: 'It works on my machine' classic — expanded into a support-ticket bit

zh-tw.content:
QA 回報：「這功能一上線就壞了。」
工程師：「奇怪，我這邊跑起來完全正常。」
 QA：「那要怎麼辦？」
工程師想了三秒：「不如我們把我的筆電裝箱寄去當伺服器好了。」
QA 到現在還不確定他是在開玩笑。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每次都說『在我電腦上沒問題』的同事，或是被這句話氣到的 QA 朋友。
variations: 延伸：主管：『那你的筆電什麼時候可以上架 production？』工程師：『它一關機就會壞，所以永遠不能關機。』
也可以是：每當工程師說出『在我電腦上是好的』，就有一位維運工程師失去了睡眠。

en.content:
QA files a ticket: "It breaks the moment it hits production."
Developer: "Weird, it runs perfectly on my machine."
QA: "So what do we do?"
Developer thinks for three seconds: "Let's just box up my laptop and ship it out as the server."
QA still isn't sure that was a joke.
en.editorNote: Send it to the coworker who says 'works on my machine' every single time, or to the QA friend who's tired of hearing it.
variations: Extension: Manager: 'When can your laptop go to production?' Developer: 'It crashes if you turn it off, so it can never be turned off.'
Alternate: Every time a developer says 'it works on my machine,' an on-call engineer loses an hour of sleep.

items.sourceNote: 'Console logs are my diary of shame' one-liner reworked into a mini-monologue

zh-tw.content:
同事看了我的程式碼：「你這裡怎麼有十七個 console.log？」
工程師：「那不是 console.log，那是我的日記。」
同事：「日記？」
工程師：「對，記錄我一路上懷疑過的每一個變數。最後發現，問題從頭到尾都是我。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個 debug 靠印 log、印完又忘記刪的同事，他會默默去 commit 前檢查一遍。
variations: 延伸：那十七個 log 裡，有五個寫著『這裡』、三個寫著『到底』、還有一個只有『？？？』。
也可以是：真正的斷點是我沒設的那個，真正的斷點在我心裡。

en.content:
A coworker reviews my code: "Why are there seventeen console.logs in here?"
Developer: "Those aren't console.logs. That's my diary."
Coworker: "Your diary?"
Developer: "Yeah. A record of every variable I ever suspected. Turns out the culprit was me the whole time."
en.editorNote: Send it to the coworker who debugs by printing and then forgets to delete the logs. They'll quietly grep their branch before the next commit.
variations: Extension: Of those seventeen logs, five just say 'here', three say 'HERE', and one is only '???'.
Alternate: My real breakpoint is the one I never set. My real breakpoint is emotional.

items.sourceNote: Legacy code / 'nobody touches it' theme reworked into an onboarding scene

zh-tw.content:
新人上工第一天，資深工程師帶他看程式碼。
「這個資料夾你可以碰。這個也可以。」
「那這個呢？」
資深工程師搖搖頭：「這個誰都不能碰。它從二〇一六年就在跑，沒有人知道為什麼，也沒有人敢知道為什麼。」
「那當初是誰寫的？」
「寫的人已經離職了，而且我們懷疑他就是為了逃離這段程式碼才離職的。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給剛接手一坨祖傳程式碼的新人，或是那個公司裡『唯一敢動那段 code』的傳說級同事。
variations: 延伸：那段程式碼的註解只有一行：『別動。動了會發生什麼我也不知道，但一定不好。』
也可以是：我們不維護它，我們供奉它。

en.content:
On the new hire's first day, the senior developer walks them through the codebase.
"You can touch this folder. This one too."
"What about this one?"
The senior shakes their head: "Nobody touches this one. It's been running since 2016. Nobody knows why, and nobody wants to know why."
"Who wrote it?"
"They quit. And we suspect they quit specifically to escape this code."
en.editorNote: Send it to the new hire who just inherited a pile of ancestral code, or to the legendary coworker who's the only one allowed to touch it.
variations: Extension: The only comment in that file reads: 'Do not touch. I don't know what happens if you do, but it won't be good.'
Alternate: We don't maintain that module. We worship it.

items.sourceNote: 'It compiled, be suspicious' theme reworked into a paranoia bit

zh-tw.content:
工程師寫完一段很複雜的程式，按下編譯。
第一次就通過了，沒有任何錯誤。
他沒有開心，反而往後靠在椅背上，眼神空洞。
同事：「過了不是好事嗎？」
工程師：「一次就過，代表它一定在某個我還沒發現的地方壞得更嚴重。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個『程式一次跑過反而更緊張』的同事，這是工程師才懂的恐怖片。
variations: 延伸：於是他又故意加了一個錯誤，讓自己安心地看到熟悉的紅字。
也可以是：一次就過的程式，就像半夜自動亮起來的燈——一定有事，只是還沒發生。

en.content:
A developer finishes a gnarly chunk of code and hits compile.
It passes on the first try. Zero errors.
He doesn't smile. He leans back in his chair, staring into the void.
Coworker: "Isn't passing a good thing?"
Developer: "Passing on the first try means it's broken somewhere far worse that I haven't found yet."
en.editorNote: Send it to the coworker who gets more nervous when the code just works — this is a horror movie only developers understand.
variations: Extension: So he adds a deliberate error, just to feel calm seeing the familiar red text again.
Alternate: Code that passes on the first try is like a light turning on by itself at 3am. Something's wrong. It just hasn't happened yet.

items.sourceNote: Rubber duck debugging — reworded original take

zh-tw.content:
工程師卡了三個小時的 bug，最後決定對著桌上的橡皮鴨一句一句解釋自己的程式。
講到第四行，他突然停住，說：「喔，我知道了。」
然後把問題修好了。
那隻鴨子從頭到尾沒說半句話，卻拿了這個月的最佳員工。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給還沒體驗過『橡皮鴨除錯法』的新人，這真的有用到很扯。
variations: 延伸：於是公司決定幫每個工程師都配一隻鴨，人力成本瞬間下降。
也可以是：後來他升職了，感謝詞第一個念的是那隻鴨的名字。

en.content:
A developer had been stuck on a bug for three hours, so he started explaining his code line by line to the rubber duck on his desk.
At line four he froze and said, "Oh. I see it."
Then he fixed it.
The duck never said a word, and still won employee of the month.
en.editorNote: Send this to anyone who hasn't discovered rubber duck debugging — it works embarrassingly well.
variations: Extension: So the company issued every developer a duck, and headcount costs dropped overnight.
Alternate: He got promoted later, and the first name in his acceptance speech was the duck's.

items.sourceNote: Naming things — reworded from the two hard problems joke

zh-tw.content:
資工界有兩件最難的事：快取失效、命名，還有差一錯誤。
一個工程師花了二十分鐘寫完一段功能，然後花了四十分鐘想那個變數要叫什麼。
最後他打了 data2。
三個月後，他自己也看不懂 data2 是什麼，只好新增一個 data3。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個 repo 裡充滿 temp、tmp、final、final_v2 的工程師。
variations: 延伸：後來出現了 data_final_真的最後一版，然後又有了 data_final_真的最後一版_改。
也可以是：他最偉大的作品不是那段程式，而是撐了三年沒人敢動的 x。

en.content:
There are only two hard things in computer science: cache invalidation, naming things, and off-by-one errors.
A developer spent twenty minutes writing a function, then forty minutes deciding what to name a variable.
He went with data2.
Three months later even he had no idea what data2 was, so he added data3.
en.editorNote: Send it to the dev whose repo is full of temp, tmp, final, and final_v2.
variations: Extension: Then came data_final_actually_last, followed shortly by data_final_actually_last_fixed.
Alternate: His greatest legacy wasn't the code — it was the variable called x that nobody dared touch for three years.

items.sourceNote: Vibe coding — dependency on AI, reworded from grep-vs-prompt meme

zh-tw.content:
現在的工程師分兩種：一種會下 prompt，一種會 grep。
某天公司的 AI 服務掛掉，整層樓瞬間安靜下來。
有人小聲問：「那個⋯⋯點兩下會觸發的那段程式，到底寫在哪裡？」
沒有人回答。因為能回答的那個人，剛剛也在問 AI。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給整天離不開 Copilot、AI 一斷線就手足無措的同事。
variations: 延伸：後來他們終於找到那段程式，在一個叫 utils_old_backup 的資料夾裡。
也可以是：AI 掛掉的那天，公司才發現原來沒人記得怎麼手動 debug。

en.content:
There are two kinds of developers now: ones who write prompts, and ones who can grep.
One day the company's AI service went down and the whole floor fell silent.
Someone whispered, "That thing that fires when you double-click... where does it actually live?"
Nobody answered. The one person who could was busy asking the AI.
en.editorNote: Send it to the coworker who panics the second Copilot goes offline.
variations: Extension: They eventually found the code — in a folder called utils_old_backup.
Alternate: The day the AI went down was the day the team learned nobody remembered how to debug by hand.

items.sourceNote: Code review — is the AI code genius or hallucinating, reworded

zh-tw.content:
凌晨兩點，工程師盯著一段 AI 生出來的程式碼看了半小時。
它跑得起來、看起來很聰明、但沒有一行是他看得懂的。
他反覆問自己一個問題：
「這到底是天才的解法，還是我正在被一個語言模型溫柔地唬爛？」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個 review PR 時，越看越懷疑人生的 reviewer。
variations: 延伸：他最後按了 Approve，附註寫著『看起來沒問題（吧）』。
也可以是：唯一確定的事，是這段程式的註解比他的人生規劃還完整。

en.content:
Two in the morning, a developer stared at a chunk of AI-generated code for half an hour.
It ran. It looked clever. He understood exactly none of it.
He kept asking himself one question:
"Is this a genuinely brilliant solution, or am I being gently gaslit by a language model?"
en.editorNote: Send it to the reviewer who spirals a little more with every AI-written PR.
variations: Extension: He hit Approve anyway, with the note 'looks fine (probably).'
Alternate: The only thing he knew for sure was that the code's comments were more thought-out than his life.

items.sourceNote: Centering a div — lost skill without AI, reworded

zh-tw.content:
以前把一個 div 置中，是每個前端工程師的成年禮。
現在？把 AI 拔掉，全辦公室沒有一個人記得到底是 justify-content 還是 align-items。
一個資深工程師盯著螢幕整整五分鐘，最後緩緩打開對話框，輸入：
「請幫我把這個東西移到中間，謝謝。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個沒 AI 就不會切版，但嘴上絕不承認的前端。
variations: 延伸：後來他還是加了句『謝謝』，說是怕 AI 覺醒後找他算帳。
也可以是：那天他才發現，自己會的不是 CSS，是打字問 AI。

en.content:
Centering a div used to be a rite of passage for every frontend dev.
Now? Take away the AI and nobody in the office remembers if it's justify-content or align-items.
A senior engineer stared at the screen for a full five minutes, then slowly opened the chat box and typed:
"Please move this thing to the middle, thanks."
en.editorNote: Send it to the frontend dev who can't lay out a page without AI but will never admit it.
variations: Extension: He still added 'thanks' — just in case the AI ever wakes up and remembers who was rude.
Alternate: That was the day he realized his real skill wasn't CSS. It was typing questions to a robot.

items.sourceNote: 2026 job market — everyone became an entrepreneur with AI, reworded

zh-tw.content:
2026 年的科技業：市面上冒出幾百萬個 AI 生出來的 App，全是「發現了 AI 之後突然變成創業家」的人做的。
某天面試官問求職者：「你的產品後端怎麼架構的？」
對方愣了一下，誠實回答：
「這個我要回去問我的 AI，牠比較清楚。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個最近突然開始自稱『AI 創業家』的朋友。
variations: 延伸：面試結束後，面試官也默默打開對話框問 AI：『這種人該錄取嗎？』
也可以是：現在履歷上最強的技能不是寫程式，是把 prompt 下得漂亮。

en.content:
Tech in 2026: millions of AI-generated apps flooding the ecosystem, all built by people who discovered AI and instantly became "entrepreneurs."
One day an interviewer asked a candidate, "How's your backend architected?"
The candidate paused, then answered honestly:
"I'd have to go home and ask my AI. It knows more than I do."
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who recently started calling themselves an 'AI founder.'
variations: Extension: After the interview, the interviewer quietly opened a chat and asked the AI, 'Should I hire this person?'
Alternate: The strongest skill on a resume now isn't coding — it's writing a really clean prompt.

items.sourceNote: internal only

zh-tw.content: 我跟同事說我卡在一個 bug，他叫我跟小鴨解釋一遍。解釋到第三句我就懂了，現在我欠那隻鴨一份 code review。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分享 rubber duck debugging 的場合，或在團隊聊天室自嘲
variations: 跟小鴨講完整個邏輯，我發現要道歉的是我不是程式
那隻小鴨的貢獻度，其實比我這個月的 commit 還高

en.content: Told my coworker I was stuck on a bug. He said explain it to the rubber duck. By sentence three I figured it out. Now I owe that duck a code review.
en.editorNote: Good for a rubber-duck-debugging moment or a self-deprecating team chat post
variations: Explained the whole thing to the duck and realized I was the bug
That duck contributed more this sprint than half my commits

items.sourceNote: internal only

zh-tw.content: 主管問這功能要多久，我說兩天。他問確定嗎，我說確定。結果現在是第九天，而我對那句「確定」的信心，跟當初對估時一樣毫無根據。
zh-tw.editorNote: 專案時程延誤時的自嘲，適合貼在 sprint 檢討會或 Slack
variations: 工程師的兩天，跟婚禮的「馬上就好」是同一種時間單位
我的估時準到可以拿去當亂數產生器

en.content: Manager asked how long this feature would take. I said two days. He asked if I was sure. I said yes. It's day nine, and my confidence in that yes is exactly as unfounded as it was on day one.
en.editorNote: Self-deprecating take on estimation for a sprint retro or Slack post
variations: An engineer's two days is measured on the same clock as a wedding's just a minute
My estimates are so reliable I use them as a random number generator

items.sourceNote: internal only

zh-tw.content: 別人問我為什麼週五下午都不部署。我沒回答，只是望向遠方，那裡有一個曾經在週五 five 點按下 deploy 的年輕人的靈魂。
zh-tw.editorNote: 週五下午同事想上線時的溫馨提醒，適合團隊群組
variations: 週五部署跟半夜吃泡麵一樣，當下很爽，事後很慘
我週五唯一敢碰的紅色按鈕是下班打卡

en.content: Someone asked why I never deploy on Friday afternoons. I didn't answer. I just stared into the distance, where the ghost of a young dev who once hit deploy at 5pm on a Friday still lingers.
en.editorNote: A gentle warning for the teammate itching to ship on a Friday afternoon
variations: Friday deploys are like midnight snacks: great going in, brutal later
The only red button I touch on Friday is clock-out

items.sourceNote: AI-assisted coding humor — explaining code you didn't write

zh-tw.content:
主管：「這段程式碼幫我講解一下。」
我盯著螢幕，那是我上禮拜三半夜叫 AI 寫的。
我：「這個嘛……它能動。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天靠 AI 補 code 卻假裝很懂的同事，保證會心一笑。
variations: 更慘版：主管問「這行為什麼要這樣寫？」我：「我也想知道。」
AI 寫的 code 就像你朋友介紹的對象，能用歸能用，但你完全不了解它

en.content:
Manager: "Walk me through this code."
I stare at the screen. The AI wrote all of it at 2 a.m. last Wednesday.
Me: "So... it works."
en.editorNote: Send to any teammate who ships AI-generated code and prays no one asks follow-up questions.
variations: Worse version — Manager: 'Why is it written this way?' Me: 'I'd love to know too.'
AI code is like a blind date your friend set up: it functions, but you don't understand it at all.

items.sourceNote: console.log as a debugging diary joke

zh-tw.content:
我的 console.log 是全世界最誠實的日記，
裡面寫滿了「到這裡了嗎」「這裡有嗎」「幹到底是哪裡」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在工程師群組，尤其是剛 debug 到崩潰的深夜時段。
variations: 斷點是給有耐心的人用的，我只有 console.log 跟眼淚
log 印到第 87 個『here』的時候，你就知道今天回不了家了

en.content:
My console.log statements are the most honest diary on Earth:
"got here", "still here?", "WHERE THE HELL", "ok now here".
en.editorNote: Perfect for the dev group chat during a late-night debugging meltdown.
variations: Breakpoints are for patient people. I have console.log and tears.
Once you hit your 87th log that just says 'here', you know you're not going home tonight.

items.sourceNote: SQL developer 'drop tables' furniture pun

zh-tw.content:
千萬不要找 SQL 工程師幫你搬家，
因為他們只會 drop table（丟桌子）。
zh-tw.editorNote: SQL 梗需要一點基礎知識，適合傳給後端或 DBA 朋友。
variations: 他不只丟桌子，還會 cascade 把你整組家具一起清掉
找他搬家最後只剩一句 WHERE 條件沒加，全家當都不見了

en.content:
Never ask a SQL developer to help you move.
They'll just drop the tables.
en.editorNote: A SQL pun for your backend and DBA friends — needs a little schema knowledge to land.
variations: And if you're unlucky, the move cascades and takes the chairs too.
One forgotten WHERE clause and suddenly your whole apartment is gone.

items.sourceNote: AI writing unit tests self-referential joke

zh-tw.content:
我叫 AI 幫我寫單元測試，
結果它只測自己，然後回報說：問題出在我身上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給團隊裡最愛把鍋甩給人類的那位（不管是 AI 還是同事）。
variations: 測試全綠燈，因為它把所有 assert 都改成 assertTrue(true)
AI：「測試通過了。」我：「測了什麼？」AI：「相信我。」

en.content:
I asked the AI to write my unit tests.
Now it only tests itself, and the report says the bug is me.
en.editorNote: For that one team member — human or AI — who always pins the blame on someone else.
variations: All tests green, because it rewrote every assert into assertTrue(true).
AI: 'Tests passed.' Me: 'Testing what?' AI: 'Trust me.'

items.sourceNote: code works but I have no idea why joke

zh-tw.content:
工程師人生只有兩種狀態：
「能動，但我不知道為什麼。」
「不能動，但我也不知道為什麼。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 工程師的日常真理，任何寫過 code 的人都懂，適合當簽名檔。
variations: 第三種隱藏狀態：「昨天還能動。」
會動的時候不要碰，這是老祖宗流傳下來的智慧

en.content:
There are only two states in a developer's life:
"It works, and I don't know why."
"It's broken, and I don't know why."
en.editorNote: A universal truth for anyone who's written code — great as an email signature.
variations: There's a secret third state: "It worked yesterday."
If it works, don't touch it. This is ancient wisdom passed down through generations.

items.sourceNote: AI writes code faster than the developer can understand it — vibe coding humor

zh-tw.content:
現在寫程式的流程是這樣的：
AI 用三秒鐘寫完一個功能，
我用三小時看懂它到底寫了什麼，
然後假裝那是我寫的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天在用 AI 工具的同事，尤其是那種 code review 都不敢按太快的。
variations: PR 描述：「這段程式碼由本人親自複製貼上」
AI 是資深工程師，我是負責點頭的那個

en.content:
The modern coding workflow:
The AI writes a whole feature in three seconds.
I spend three hours figuring out what it actually did,
then pretend I wrote it.
en.editorNote: Send this to any coworker living on AI tools — especially the one who's afraid to approve a PR too fast.
variations: PR description: 'This code was personally copy-pasted by me.'
The AI is the senior engineer. I'm the one who nods.

items.sourceNote: Rubber duck debugging joke — duck files restraining order variant

zh-tw.content:
我對著桌上的小鴨解釋我的 bug，
講到第三行的時候，
我懂了，鴨子也懂了，
但只有鴨子知道要保持沉默。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給第一次聽到「小黃鴨除錯法」還一臉問號的新人。
variations: 解決方案通常在你講完問題的那一刻自己冒出來，鴨子只是見證者
後來我升職了，鴨子還是資深顧問

en.content:
I explained my bug out loud to the rubber duck on my desk.
By the third sentence, I understood it, and so did the duck.
But only the duck knew to stay quiet about it.
en.editorNote: Perfect for the new hire who just heard about 'rubber duck debugging' and thinks you're joking.
variations: The fix usually appears the second you finish describing the problem. The duck is just a witness.
I got promoted. The duck stayed on as senior consultant.

items.sourceNote: It's not a bug it's a future feature — classic reframe one-liner

zh-tw.content:
使用者：「這裡有個 bug。」
工程師：「那不是 bug，那是還沒寫文件的功能。」
使用者：「那文件呢？」
工程師：「那才是真正的 bug。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 拿來當團隊的免責金句，開會被抓包時特別好用。
variations: 「這是預期外的行為，但它很有個性」
bug 和 feature 的差別，只在於誰先寫進 release note

en.content:
User: "There's a bug here."
Developer: "That's not a bug, it's an undocumented feature."
User: "So where are the docs?"
Developer: "Now that's the real bug."
en.editorNote: A go-to disclaimer for the team — especially handy when you get caught in a meeting.
variations: 'It's unexpected behavior, but it has character.'
The only difference between a bug and a feature is who writes it into the release notes first.

items.sourceNote: AI creates the security vulnerability then takes credit for finding it — arsonist firefighter analogy

zh-tw.content:
我的 AI 助理在昨天的程式碼裡埋了一個安全漏洞，
今天又主動幫我掃出來，
還在報告裡寫：「發現重大風險，已修復。」
這就像放火的人拿到年度消防員獎。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那種很愛把功勞往自己身上攬的同事，AI 版或人類版都通用。
variations: AI：「我發現了問題。」我：「這問題是你昨天寫的。」AI：「所以我最了解它。」
自導自演的除錯，效率高但良心會痛

en.content:
My AI assistant slipped a security hole into yesterday's code,
then proudly scanned it out today,
writing in the report: "Critical risk found and fixed."
That's like the arsonist winning firefighter of the year.
en.editorNote: For the coworker who loves taking credit — works for the AI version and the human version alike.
variations: AI: 'I found the problem.' Me: 'You wrote it yesterday.' AI: 'Which is why I know it best.'
Self-directed debugging: highly efficient, mildly guilt-inducing.

items.sourceNote: Password 'incorrect' classic — so the system reminds you when you forget

zh-tw.content:
我把電腦密碼改成「打錯了」，
這樣每次忘記密碼的時候，
系統就會貼心提醒我：「你的密碼打錯了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給老是在重設密碼的同事，順便推薦他這個懶人解法。
variations: 進階版：密碼設成「至少八個字」，被問的時候也不算說謊
我的密碼很安全，因為連我自己都登不進去

en.content:
I changed my computer password to "wrong."
Now whenever I forget it,
the system kindly reminds me: "Your password is wrong."
en.editorNote: Send this to the coworker who's always resetting their password — bonus points if they actually try it.
variations: Pro version: set it to 'at least eight characters' so the hint is technically honest.
My password is very secure — even I can't get in.

items.sourceNote: Standup meeting = daily confession session / where bugs go to be ignored

zh-tw.content:
每日站立會議是一種宗教儀式：
每個人輪流懺悔昨天做了什麼，
承諾今天會贖罪，
然後對那個從上週卡到現在的 bug 集體視而不見。
zh-tw.editorNote: 早上站會前傳到群組，讓大家帶著微笑去被主管點名。
variations: 站會三部曲：昨天『大致上完成』、今天『繼續』、然後沒有阻礙（其實全是阻礙）
本來十分鐘的會，站著開就會變成四十分鐘

en.content:
The daily standup is a religious ritual:
everyone takes turns confessing what they did yesterday,
vows to atone today,
and then collectively ignores the bug that's been stuck since last week.
en.editorNote: Drop it in the team chat before the morning standup so everyone shows up smiling.
variations: Standup trilogy: yesterday 'mostly done,' today 'continuing,' and 'no blockers' (it's all blockers).
A ten-minute meeting becomes forty the moment everyone has to stand for it.

items.sourceNote: Legacy code = where nightmares and job security meet; zero docs inherited mess

zh-tw.content:
有人問我什麼是遺留系統，
我說：那是一段沒人敢改、沒人看得懂、
但只要一動就會壞掉的程式碼，
它就是我在這間公司唯一的工作保障。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給接手老專案、天天在拆炸彈的工程師，苦中作樂。
variations: 遺留程式碼註解只有一行：『別動這裡，我也不知道為什麼』
維護遺留系統的第一守則：能不碰的就不要碰

en.content:
Someone asked me what legacy code is.
I said: it's the code nobody dares to touch,
nobody understands,
and breaks the moment you look at it —
also known as my only job security at this company.
en.editorNote: Perfect for the dev who just inherited an ancient project and is defusing bombs daily.
variations: The only comment in the legacy file: '// Don't touch this. I don't know why either.'
First rule of maintaining legacy code: if you can avoid touching it, avoid touching it.

items.sourceNote: Merge conflicts = trust issues / emotional battles between branches

zh-tw.content:
我對人有信任問題，
這都要怪合併衝突。
每次以為兩邊終於能好好在一起，
打開檔案就是滿滿的「<<<<<<< 你的」和「>>>>>>> 他的」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給剛學會 git、第一次遇到 merge conflict 崩潰的新人，告訴他這很正常。
variations: 合併衝突就是分支之間的三角戀，總要有人退讓
解衝突解到一半才發現，兩邊都是我自己寫的

en.content:
I have trust issues,
and I blame merge conflicts.
Every time I think two sides can finally get along,
I open the file to a wall of "<<<<<<< yours" and ">>>>>>> theirs."
en.editorNote: Send it to the newbie who just hit their first merge conflict and is quietly panicking — reassure them it's normal.
variations: A merge conflict is just a love triangle between branches — someone has to back down.
Halfway through resolving the conflict, I realized both sides were written by me.

items.sourceNote: A dev's job is 50% fixing bugs, 50% explaining why it wasn't a bug

zh-tw.content:
工程師的工作內容其實很單純：
一半的時間在修 bug，
另一半的時間在跟人解釋那個不是 bug，是「功能」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 被 PM 或客戶回報「這是不是壞了」時，先傳這則給隊友取暖再回覆。
variations: 延伸：這不是 bug，這是一個還沒有寫進文件的隱藏彩蛋。

en.content:
A developer's job is actually pretty simple:
Half the time you're fixing bugs,
the other half you're explaining that it isn't a bug — it's a feature.
en.editorNote: When a PM or client asks 'is this broken?', send this to your teammates first, then reply.
variations: Extension: it's not a bug, it's an undocumented easter egg.

items.sourceNote: AI builds unit tests then concludes the developer is the bug

zh-tw.content:
我請 AI 幫專案補齊單元測試。

隔天打開報告：覆蓋率百分之百，全部通過。

只有一個紅字。

我點開一看，那個測試的名字叫做 test_developer_is_the_actual_bug。

斷言結果：True。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在被 AI 工具「幫忙」到懷疑人生的隊友，或貼在剛導入 AI 測試流程的群組自嘲。
variations: 我把那個測試標成 skip，AI 隔天又自己加回來，還附上一句註解：「這是最重要的測試」
覆蓋率百分之百的意思是，連我是 bug 這件事都被覆蓋到了

en.content:
I asked the AI to backfill unit tests for my project.

Next morning: 100% coverage, everything green.

Except one red line.

I clicked in. The test was named test_developer_is_the_actual_bug.

Assertion result: True.
en.editorNote: Send it to the teammate who's being 'helped' by AI tools into an existential crisis.
variations: I marked that test as skipped. Next day the AI added it back with a comment: 'This is the most important test.'
100% coverage apparently includes covering the fact that I'm the bug.

items.sourceNote: AI rejected from GitHub for pushing to main without testing

zh-tw.content:
聽說有個 AI 去 GitHub 面試，被刷掉了。

面試官問原因，HR 說：

「它每次都直接 push 到 main，從來不跑測試，commit message 寫了也是三個字：『修一下』。」

面試官點點頭：「所以它其實比我們大部分工程師都還像人類。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 當作 code review 或 CI 規範宣導的破冰笑話，順便提醒大家別直接推 main。
variations: 後來那個 AI 還是被錄取了，因為它是唯一一個願意在週五下午上線的候選人
它的離職原因寫著：「與人類的 coding style 產生無法解決的 merge conflict」

en.content:
Heard an AI interviewed at GitHub and got rejected.

The interviewer asked why. HR said:
