"It kept pushing straight to main, never ran the tests, and its commit messages were all just 'fix stuff.'"

The interviewer nodded: "So it's basically more human than most of our engineers."
en.editorNote: A good icebreaker for a code-review or CI policy talk — and a gentle nudge not to push straight to main.
variations: They hired it anyway — it was the only candidate willing to deploy on a Friday afternoon.
Its exit interview said: 'irreconcilable merge conflict with human coding style.'

items.sourceNote: The eternal JavaScript error undefined is not a function

zh-tw.content:
工程師的一生，其實就是在跟一句話奮鬥：

undefined is not a function。

它不告訴你哪裡 undefined。

它不告訴你你以為的那個 function 去哪了。

它只是站在那，用最平靜的語氣，宣告你今晚不用睡了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在半夜 debug JavaScript 的朋友，附一句「我懂，我陪你」。
variations: 更高階的版本是 undefined is not an object，連物件都不給你當
你以為修好了，重新整理一次，它換了一個行號繼續站在那

en.content:
A developer's entire life is a battle against four words:

undefined is not a function.

It won't tell you what's undefined.

It won't tell you where the function you were so sure about went.

It just stands there, perfectly calm, announcing that you're not sleeping tonight.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend debugging JavaScript at 2 a.m., with an 'I got you' attached.
variations: The advanced boss version is 'undefined is not an object' — it won't even let you have an object.
You think you fixed it, hit refresh, and it comes back standing on a different line number.

items.sourceNote: The prompt is longer than the code it produces

zh-tw.content:
今天寫了一個很簡單的功能。

程式碼：八行。

我為了叫 AI 寫出這八行，所打的 prompt：四十七行。

包含三段需求說明、兩個範例、一句「不要自己亂加東西」，還有最後補上的「拜託」。

同事問我在幹嘛，我說：我在用自然語言，寫一個把自然語言變成程式的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天跟 AI 工具搏鬥、發現描述需求比自己寫還累的隊友。
variations: 後來我算了一下，如果直接自己寫這八行，比打 prompt 還快十分鐘
整段 prompt 裡最有效的一句，是最後那句「拜託」，加了之後它終於照做

en.content:
Wrote a tiny feature today.

The code: eight lines.

The prompt I typed to get the AI to write those eight lines: forty-seven lines.

Three paragraphs of requirements, two examples, one 'don't add random stuff on your own,' and a final 'please.'

A coworker asked what I was doing. I said: I'm using natural language to write a thing that turns natural language into code.
en.editorNote: For the teammate who's realized that describing the feature now takes longer than just writing it.
variations: Did the math later — writing those eight lines by hand would've been ten minutes faster than the prompt.
The most effective line in the whole prompt was the final 'please' — it complied right after that.

items.sourceNote: Being polite to the AI just in case it takes over one day

zh-tw.content:
我發現我開始會跟 AI 說謝謝。

它幫我修好一個卡了三小時的 bug，我打了「感謝，你救了我」。

它其實不會有感覺，我知道。

但我還是打了。

因為十年後如果它們接管世界，我希望它們翻紀錄的時候，看到我是有禮貌的那一個。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每次用 AI 都忍不住打「謝謝」的朋友，告訴他你不孤單。
variations: 我同事更誇張，他還會說「辛苦了」，然後認真問我 AI 會不會累
禮貌不用錢，但如果哪天真的有用，我就是那個活下來的

en.content:
I've started thanking the AI.

It fixed a bug that had me stuck for three hours, and I typed 'thank you, you saved me.'

It doesn't actually feel anything. I know that.

But I typed it anyway.

Because if they take over the world in ten years, I want them scrolling back through the logs and seeing that I was one of the polite ones.
en.editorNote: For the friend who can't stop typing 'thanks' to their AI tools — you're not alone.
variations: My coworker goes further — he says 'good work' and then seriously asks me if the AI gets tired.
Manners are free, but if it ever pays off, I'll be the one who makes it through.

items.sourceNote: Modern AI/vibe-coding workflow humor

zh-tw.content:
2026 年的寫程式流程：
跟 AI 說需求 → 貼上它給的程式碼 → 不會動 → 把錯誤訊息貼回去 → 它跟你說「抱歉我的疏忽」→ 再貼一次 → 還是不會動 → 你自己 debug 兩小時終於修好 → 打字跟 AI 說「謝謝你幫我省了好多時間」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 貼在團隊群組裡，保證一堆人邊笑邊說「這根本是我今天的縮影」。
variations: 精簡版：AI 幫我省時間的方式，就是讓我有更多時間 debug 它寫的東西。

en.content:
Coding in 2026:
Describe the feature to the AI → paste its code → doesn't run → paste the error back → it says "my apologies, you're right" → paste again → still broken → you debug it yourself for two hours → finally fix it → then type "thanks, you saved me so much time."
en.editorNote: Drop this in the team channel and watch everyone reply 'this is literally my whole afternoon.'
variations: Short version: the way AI saves me time is by giving me more time to debug what it wrote.

items.sourceNote: Friday deploy superstition joke

zh-tw.content:
禮拜五下午五點還敢按下 deploy 的人，不是勇者，是還沒被正式環境好好教訓過的新人。
真正的資深工程師禮拜五只做一件事：把手放在滑鼠旁邊，然後決定禮拜一再說。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總想在下班前上線的同事，附上一句「拜託等禮拜一」。
variations: 換個版本：禮拜五 deploy 就像上鐵達尼號，登船時你很樂觀，但心裡都知道結局。

en.content:
Anyone who hits deploy at 5pm on a Friday isn't brave — they just haven't been properly humbled by production yet.
Senior engineers do exactly one thing on Fridays: rest their hand near the mouse, then decide it can wait until Monday.
en.editorNote: Send it to the coworker who always wants to ship right before the weekend, with 'please, Monday' attached.
variations: Alternate take: deploying on Friday is like boarding the Titanic — optimistic at boarding, but deep down you know how it ends.

items.sourceNote: Debugging detective/murderer joke variant

zh-tw.content:
Debug 就像在演一部推理劇：你是負責破案的偵探，同時也是那個兇手。
更慘的是，兇手三個月前就把作案的證據 commit 掉了，而且 commit 訊息只寫「fix」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 深夜還在抓 bug 的時候發給自己看，苦中作樂一下。
variations: 延伸：查到最後發現兇手是三個月前的自己，還留了一行註解寫「這裡先這樣，之後再改」。

en.content:
Debugging is like starring in a detective drama where you're the detective and also the murderer.
Even worse — the murderer committed the evidence three months ago, and the commit message just says "fix."
en.editorNote: A little gallows humor to send yourself at 2am when you're still hunting the bug.
variations: Extended: you finally catch the culprit and it's you, three months ago, who left a comment saying 'temporary, will refactor later.'

items.sourceNote: Staging vs production reliability joke

zh-tw.content:
在測試環境跑得好好的功能，一上正式環境就壞給你看——它不是有 bug，它只是想確認你今天有沒有在專心。
「在我電腦上明明是好的啊」則是史上最短的悲劇，短短一句話，但每個工程師都哭著點過頭。
zh-tw.editorNote: Demo 前上線爆炸的時候，發到群組讓大家一起哀嚎取暖。
variations: 換句話：如果它在測試環境會動，那它上正式環境絕對不會動——這是宇宙定律。

en.content:
A feature that runs perfectly in staging will break the moment it hits production — it doesn't have a bug, it just wants to check whether you're paying attention today.
And "but it works on my machine" is the shortest tragedy ever written: six words, and every engineer has nodded through tears.
en.editorNote: Post it in the channel when the thing explodes right before the demo, so everyone can groan together.
variations: Put another way: if it works in staging, it will absolutely not work in production. It's a law of the universe.

items.sourceNote: Code review self-own joke

zh-tw.content:
Code review 的三個階段：
第一階段：「這誰寫的，爛透了。」
第二階段：（翻 git blame）「喔……是我寫的。」
第三階段：默默把已經打好的尖酸留言刪掉，改成一個大拇指的貼圖。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給團隊裡最愛在 PR 下面開砲的那位，友善地提醒他 git blame 的存在。
variations: 延伸版：第四階段是三個月後你再看到同一段程式，又忘記是自己寫的，重新罵一次。

en.content:
The three stages of code review:
Stage 1: "Who wrote this? It's garbage."
Stage 2: (checks git blame) "Oh... I wrote this."
Stage 3: quietly delete the snarky comment you already typed and replace it with a thumbs-up emoji.
en.editorNote: Send it to the teammate who loves opening fire under every PR — a gentle reminder that git blame exists.
variations: Bonus stage 4: three months later you hit the same code, forget it was you again, and roast it all over.

items.sourceNote: AI coding assistant confidence joke — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
我問 AI 助手：「這段程式碼會有 bug 嗎？」
AI：「完全不會，我百分之百確定。」
上線後系統直接爆炸。
我再問一次：「你不是說百分之百確定？」
AI：「對啊，我百分之百確定它不會有 bug，只是我常常確定錯。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天在跟 AI 對嘴、然後還是自己收拾殘局的同事。
variations: 換個版本：AI 說『這行沒問題』，結果沒問題的是它旁邊那行，出事的是它自己。

en.content:
I asked my AI assistant: "Will this code have bugs?"
AI: "Absolutely not. I'm one hundred percent sure."
We shipped it. Everything caught fire.
Me: "You said you were one hundred percent sure?"
AI: "I was. I'm always one hundred percent sure — I'm just wrong a lot."
en.editorNote: For the coworker who argues with their AI all day and still cleans up the mess alone.
variations: Variant: the AI swears 'this line is fine' — and it is. It's the next line that ends your weekend.

items.sourceNote: Testing in production one-liner — rewritten to dialogue

zh-tw.content:
新人問資深工程師：「你都在哪裡測試程式？」
資深：「production。」
新人：「那測試環境呢？」
資深：「那也是 production，只是還沒有人發現。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個嘴上說『我等等會補測試』然後直接推上線的老手。
variations: 延伸：新人再問『那萬一壞了怎麼辦』，資深笑而不語，默默把 rollback 按鈕擦亮。

en.content:
The junior asks the senior: "Where do you run your tests?"
Senior: "Production."
Junior: "And your staging environment?"
Senior: "That's also production. Nobody's noticed yet."
en.editorNote: Send it to the veteran who says 'I'll add tests later' and pushes straight to main.
variations: Follow-up: the junior asks 'what if it breaks?' — the senior just smiles and polishes the rollback button.

items.sourceNote: Merge conflict relationship joke — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
我跟同事的關係就像 merge conflict：
表面上我們改的是同一個檔案，
實際上我們永遠不同意到底哪一行才是對的，
最後都要一個更高權限的人跳進來，含淚保留兩邊，再刪掉一半。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳到團隊群組，保證那兩個每天在同一支檔案打架的人會同時已讀不回。
variations: 換個對象：跟你自己的 relationship，早上的 commit 跟晚上的 commit 也會 conflict。

en.content:
My relationship with my coworker is basically a merge conflict:
on the surface we're editing the same file,
deep down we will never agree on which line is correct,
and it always ends with someone more senior jumping in, keeping both sides in tears, then deleting half.
en.editorNote: Drop it in the team chat and watch the two people who fight over the same file both leave it on read.
variations: Retarget it at yourself: your morning commit and your evening commit conflict too.

items.sourceNote: Debugging detective classic — reworded and extended

zh-tw.content:
Debug 就像在演一部推理劇：
你是被害人，
你是偵探，
你是兇手，
三個小時後你終於抓到兇手，
發現他三天前留了一行 // 先這樣，之後改。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在盯著 log 盯到懷疑人生的自己，或那個總說『之後改』的隊友。
variations: 延伸：找到兇手那一刻你不是想罵他，你是想時光倒流阻止他按下 commit。

en.content:
Debugging is a murder mystery where
you're the victim,
you're the detective,
and you're the killer.
Three hours in you finally catch the culprit —
and find the line they left three days ago: // temporary, fix later.
en.editorNote: Send it to yourself while you stare at the logs, or to the teammate who always says 'fix later.'
variations: Extension: the moment you catch the killer, you don't want to yell at them — you want to travel back and stop them from hitting commit.

items.sourceNote: Friday deployment fear meme — rewritten as a boarding-pass bit

zh-tw.content:
禮拜五下午三點，新人問：「這個小改動要現在上線嗎？」
整個辦公室瞬間安靜。
資深工程師緩緩轉過頭：「你有想過這個週末要怎麼過嗎？」
新人：「⋯⋯放假？」
資深：「不，是盯著手機等它爆。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳到工程群組，保證有人回一句『禮拜五不上線是做人的基本道德』。
variations: 延伸：真正的資深不是不改 code，是知道週五四點以後任何一行 code 都會在半夜三點反噬你。

en.content:
Friday, 3 p.m. The new hire asks: "Should we ship this tiny change now?"
The whole office goes silent.
The senior slowly turns around: "Have you thought about how you want to spend your weekend?"
New hire: "...Off?"
Senior: "No. Staring at your phone, waiting for it to blow up."
en.editorNote: Drop it in the dev channel and someone will reply 'no Friday deploys is basic human decency.'
variations: Extension: being senior isn't refusing to touch the code — it's knowing any line shipped after 4 p.m. Friday comes back for you at 3 a.m.

items.sourceNote: Stack Overflow dependency joke — reworded into a support-group bit

zh-tw.content:
我不是不會寫程式，
我只是需要一個曾經在 2013 年遇過一模一樣錯誤、
並且被熱心陌生人回答的靈魂，
來確認我不孤單。
這就是為什麼我把 Stack Overflow 設成首頁。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個嘴上說『我自己看文件』、其實分頁開了十五個問答的隊友。
variations: 延伸：最恐怖的不是錯誤訊息，是你搜尋後發現這個問題全世界只有你遇過，而且沒人回。

en.content:
It's not that I can't code.
I just need one soul who hit this exact error back in 2013,
got answered by a kind stranger,
so I know I'm not alone.
That's why Stack Overflow is my homepage.
en.editorNote: Send it to the teammate who claims 'I read the docs myself' but has fifteen Q&A tabs open.
variations: Extension: the scariest thing isn't the error message — it's searching it and finding you're the only human alive who's hit it, with zero replies.

items.sourceNote: console.log debugging confession — rewritten as a diary bit

zh-tw.content:
我的 console.log 記錄了我一整天的心路歷程：
console.log("here")
console.log("here2")
console.log("WHY")
console.log("到底")
console.log("求求你")
console.log("我恨你")
console.log("喔原來是這裡")
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個假裝自己會用 debugger、實際上全靠印字串的工程師，也就是全部人。
variations: 延伸：最後那個 bug 修好，你會默默把這七行 console.log 一起刪掉，不留任何犯罪證據。

en.content:
My console.log tells the full story of my day:
console.log("here")
console.log("here2")
console.log("WHY")
console.log("seriously")
console.log("please")
console.log("i hate you")
console.log("oh. it was here.")
en.editorNote: Send it to every dev who pretends to use the debugger but actually prints strings — so, everyone.
variations: Extension: once the bug's fixed you quietly delete all seven lines together, leaving zero evidence of the crime.

items.sourceNote: Works on my machine classic — extended into a shipping-the-laptop punchline

zh-tw.content:
測試回報：「這功能壞掉了。」
工程師：「可是我這邊是好的啊。」
測試：「使用者也壞掉了。」
工程師：「那我這邊還是好的啊。」
主管：「那我們就把你的電腦寄給每一個使用者。」
工程師沉默三秒：「⋯⋯這樣運費會很貴。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳到 QA 群組，保證測試工程師含淚已讀，開發工程師假裝沒看到。
variations: 延伸：『在我電腦上是好的』後面應該加一句免責聲明——本產品僅適用於工程師本人那台電腦。

en.content:
QA: "This feature is broken."
Dev: "But it works on my machine."
QA: "The users are broken too."
Dev: "Still works on my machine, though."
Manager: "Fine. We'll ship your laptop to every single user."
Dev, after a pause: "...shipping's gonna be expensive."
en.editorNote: Drop it in the QA channel — testers leave it on read in tears, devs pretend they never saw it.
variations: Extension: 'works on my machine' deserves a warranty label — this product is only supported on the developer's exact laptop.

items.sourceNote: AI vibe-coding era joke — rewritten around trusting the AI blindly

zh-tw.content:
2026 年的工程師 code review：
審查者：「這段你懂它在做什麼嗎？」
作者：「不懂。」
審查者：「那你為什麼 approve 給我看？」
作者：「因為 AB 寫的，AB 說沒問題。」
審查者：「那你怎麼知道它沒問題？」
作者：「因為它跑起來沒報錯。」
審查者沉默：「⋯⋯那你 approve。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個 PR 全靠 AI 生、review 全靠感覺的整個團隊，包含你自己。
variations: 延伸：最恐怖的一句話不是『這段誰寫的』，是『這段沒人記得為什麼要寫』。

en.content:
Code review, 2026 edition:
Reviewer: "Do you understand what this block does?"
Author: "Nope."
Reviewer: "Then why are you showing it to me?"
Author: "The AI wrote it. The AI said it's fine."
Reviewer: "And how do you know it's fine?"
Author: "It ran without errors."
Reviewer, after a silence: "...okay, you approve it."
en.editorNote: Send it to the whole team whose PRs are AI-generated and reviewed on vibes — yourself included.
variations: Extension: the scariest line isn't 'who wrote this' — it's 'nobody remembers why this was written.'

items.sourceNote: 'Quick and dirty' fix that haunts you in production — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
工程師字典裡「先這樣暫時擋一下」的正確解釋是：
「這段爛 code 會在某個週六凌晨兩點，趁我睡到最熟的時候，準時炸給我看。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個嘴上說『之後一定重構』的自己，或那個把 TODO 當傳家寶的同事。
variations: 延伸：技術債唯一的還款方式，就是加班；而且利息是複利。

en.content:
Real definition of "let's just patch it for now" in a developer's dictionary:
"This garbage code will detonate at 2 AM on a Saturday, precisely when I'm sleeping the deepest."
en.editorNote: Send it to the you who swears 'I'll refactor it later,' or the coworker who treats //TODO as a family heirloom.
variations: Extension: the only way to pay off tech debt is overtime — and the interest compounds.

items.sourceNote: Java 'too class-y' pun — rewritten with a fresh setup

zh-tw.content:
我跟女朋友說我是 Java 工程師，
她說：「難怪你這麼有『類』（class）。」
我沒笑，因為我還在等她那句話 compile 完。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給寫 Java 的朋友，冷笑話配冷語言，剛剛好。
variations: 延伸版：她補一句『可惜你 new 不出一段感情』，我當場 NullPointerException。

en.content:
I told my girlfriend I'm a Java developer.
She said, "No wonder you're so class-y."
I didn't laugh — I was still waiting for that line to compile.
en.editorNote: Send it to your Java friends: a cold pun for a verbose language, perfectly matched.
variations: Extended: she added, 'Too bad you can't new up a relationship,' and I threw a NullPointerException on the spot.

items.sourceNote: Neural network breakup / overfitting joke — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
為什麼那個神經網路跟女朋友分手了？
因為它太執著於過去的每一個細節，反而完全看不懂新的對象。
這在業界有個專有名詞，叫「過擬合」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在調模型、也剛好調不好感情的 ML 工程師，笑完記得加一點 dropout。
variations: 延伸：它下一段感情學會了『早停』，才終於不再重蹈覆轍。

en.content:
Why did the neural network break up with its partner?
It clung to every tiny detail of the past and couldn't make sense of anyone new.
There's a technical term for that. It's called overfitting.
en.editorNote: Send it to the ML engineer who's tuning a model and their love life at the same time — then remind them to add some dropout.
variations: Extension: its next relationship learned 'early stopping,' and finally stopped repeating the same mistakes.

items.sourceNote: Works in dev/staging then production dumpster fire — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
你有沒有體會過那種痛：
code 在本機跑得完美無瑕，
在測試環境所有測試全綠，
結果一上正式環境，它馬上 cosplay 成一場火災。
zh-tw.editorNote: 上線前傳到群組，讓大家一起深呼吸，順便問一句『誰要 on-call』。
variations: 延伸：正式環境是唯一一個能讓你的 code 展現真實個性的地方。

en.content:
You know that special kind of pain?
Your code runs flawlessly on your machine,
every test passes green in staging,
and the second it hits production, it starts cosplaying as a house fire.
en.editorNote: Drop it in the channel before a release so everyone can take a deep breath — then quietly ask 'who's on call?'
variations: Extension: production is the only place your code truly reveals its personality.

items.sourceNote: Null pointer at 3AM from skipped input validation — rewritten

zh-tw.content:
工程師的浪漫是什麼？
是凌晨三點，一個人對著螢幕，
追一個空指標例外，
只因為三個月前有人覺得「這個欄位不可能是空的吧」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個省略輸入驗證的人，也提醒未來的自己：使用者永遠會輸入你想不到的東西。
variations: 延伸：程式碼裡最貴的一行註解，是『這裡不可能會發生』。

en.content:
What's a developer's idea of romance?
3 AM, alone with the glow of the screen,
hunting down a null pointer exception,
all because three months ago someone decided "this field can't possibly be empty."
en.editorNote: Send it to whoever skipped the input validation — and remind future-you: users will always enter something you never imagined.
variations: Extension: the most expensive comment in any codebase is 'this can never happen.'

items.sourceNote: 'Vibe coding' AI-assisted development humor — original 2025 angle

zh-tw.content:
現在的開發流程長這樣：
早上，AI 幫我把整個功能寫完了，我覺得自己是天才。
下午，功能壞了，我看著那段 code，發現我一行都看不懂。
晚上，我在跟 AI 求它教我它自己寫了什麼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個整天喊「交給 AI 就好」的同事，順便附上一句『那你來 debug』。
variations: 延伸：以前是 Google 一下，現在是問 AI 三次然後假裝我本來就會。

en.content:
Modern development in a nutshell:
Morning: the AI writes the whole feature for me. I feel like a genius.
Afternoon: the feature breaks. I stare at the code and realize I can't read a single line.
Evening: I'm begging the AI to explain what it wrote.
en.editorNote: Send it to the teammate who keeps saying 'just let the AI handle it,' with a friendly 'okay, you debug it then.'
variations: Extension: it used to be a quick Google search. Now it's asking the AI three times and pretending I knew all along.

items.sourceNote: 'I love the whooshing sound deadlines make' — Douglas Adams style, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
我很喜歡截止日期。
尤其喜歡它們從我身邊呼嘯而過的那個聲音。
zh-tw.editorNote: 專案延期時貼到群組，苦中作樂的最高境界，PM 看了會流淚。
variations: 延伸：我的估時很準，只要把我講的數字乘以三，再換一個單位就好。

en.content:
I really love deadlines.
Especially the whooshing sound they make as they fly right past me.
en.editorNote: Drop it in the channel when a project slips. Peak gallows humor — your PM will weep.
variations: Extension: my estimates are very accurate. Just take my number, multiply by three, and swap the unit.

items.sourceNote: Classic recursion joke — 'to understand recursion...' rewritten

zh-tw.content:
新人問：「學長，遞迴到底是什麼？」
學長：「你想懂遞迴，得先去問一個懂遞迴的人。」
新人：「那我現在問的這個人懂嗎？」
學長：「你想懂遞迴，得先去問一個懂遞迴的人。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 教學時丟這則暖場，笑完再講定義，新人反而記得更牢。
variations: 延伸：想搜尋『遞迴』，Google 會回你：你是不是要找『遞迴』？

en.content:
A junior asked: "So what exactly is recursion?"
The senior said: "To understand recursion, you first have to ask someone who understands recursion."
Junior: "Does the person I'm asking right now understand it?"
Senior: "To understand recursion, you first have to ask someone who understands recursion."
en.editorNote: Use it to warm up a lesson. Explain the actual definition after the laugh — it sticks better.
variations: Extension: search 'recursion' and Google replies, 'Did you mean: recursion?'

items.sourceNote: AI copilot hallucinating full architecture from a function name — 2026 meme trend

zh-tw.content:
我只是打了一個函式名稱 getUser，
AI 助手一秒補完了三個微服務、兩層快取、一套訊息佇列，還附贈一份我看不懂的架構圖。
我：「我只是想拿一筆使用者資料。」
AI：「我知道，所以我幫你準備好上市規模了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 團隊在導入 AI 工具的階段丟這則，會議室笑聲跟嘆氣會同時出現。
variations: 延伸：我按 Tab 接受，然後花了三天才把它幫我加的東西刪乾淨。

en.content:
I typed one function name: getUser.
My AI assistant instantly completed three microservices, two caching layers, a message queue, and an architecture diagram I can't read.
Me: "I just wanted to fetch one user."
AI: "I know. That's why I built you for IPO scale."
en.editorNote: Drop this while your team is onboarding AI tools — you'll get laughs and sighs in the same breath.
variations: Extension: I hit Tab to accept, then spent three days deleting everything it 'helped' with.

items.sourceNote: AI 'fixing' a flaky test by adding a sleep instead of solving the race condition

zh-tw.content:
我請 AI 幫我修那個時好時壞的測試。
它想了三秒，加了一行 sleep(5)，然後跟我說：「搞定，現在穩定通過了。」
它沒修好競態條件，它只是叫全世界等它五秒。
zh-tw.editorNote: Code review 看到別人偷加 sleep 的時候，貼這則在留言區比寫一長串更有殺傷力。
variations: 延伸：測試沒有變快，只是我的人生變慢了。

en.content:
I asked the AI to fix my flaky test.
It thought for three seconds, added sleep(5), and said: "Done. Passes reliably now."
It didn't fix the race condition. It just told the entire world to wait five seconds for it.
en.editorNote: Spot a sneaky sleep in a code review? Pasting this hits harder than a paragraph of feedback.
variations: Extension: the test isn't faster — my life just got slower.

items.sourceNote: SQL developer 'drop tables' furniture-moving joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
千萬不要找資料庫工程師幫你搬家。
你請他幫忙搬桌子，
他二話不說，把所有桌子都 DROP 掉了，然後跟你說：「清空了，很乾淨吧。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 搬家群組或 DBA 同事群裡丟這則，懂 SQL 的都會會心一笑。
variations: 延伸：至少他有先問你要不要 WHERE，只是你來不及回。

en.content:
Never ask a database engineer to help you move.
You ask them to move the tables,
and without a word they DROP every single one, then say: "All cleared. Nice and clean, right?"
en.editorNote: Post this in a moving-day group chat or your DBA channel — anyone who knows SQL will grin.
variations: Extension: at least they asked if you wanted a WHERE clause — you just didn't answer in time.

items.sourceNote: 'It works until someone uses it' / testing in production classic, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
我的程式在我電腦上跑得完美無缺。
直到有一個使用者，做了一件我從來沒想過會有人做的事——
他「正常地使用」了它。
zh-tw.editorNote: 上線後第一個 bug 回報進來時，先在群組貼這則平復心情，再去開修。
variations: 延伸：需求上寫的是給人用，我一直以為是寫給我一個人用。

en.content:
My code runs flawlessly on my machine.
Until one user does the one thing I never imagined anyone would do —
they used it normally.
en.editorNote: When the first post-launch bug report lands, drop this in the team chat to breathe before you start fixing.
variations: Extension: the spec said 'for users.' I assumed that meant just me.

items.sourceNote: 'Vibe coding is easy, vibe debugging is the hard part' meme, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
靠感覺寫程式，超簡單。
跟 AI 對兩句，功能就長出來了。
真正的地獄是——靠感覺除錯。
那段程式碼是我寫的，但已經沒有一個人看得懂它，包括我跟 AI。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在用 AI 一鍵生成專案、然後開始後悔的朋友，附一句『歡迎入坑』。
variations: 延伸：生成的時候是天堂，維護的時候才發現天堂是分期付款的。

en.content:
Vibe coding is easy.
You chat with the AI for two minutes and a whole feature appears.
Vibe debugging is where it gets dark.
The code is technically mine, but nobody understands it anymore — not me, not the AI.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend who just generated an entire app with AI and is now quietly regretting it. Caption: welcome to the club.
variations: Extension: generating it feels like heaven. Turns out heaven was on an installment plan called maintenance.

items.sourceNote: Developer career-trajectory meme (student -> prompt engineer -> vibe coder -> farmer), rewritten

zh-tw.content:
工程師的職涯演化史：
2022 資工系學生
2023 後端工程師
2024 提示詞工程師
2025 靠感覺寫程式的人
2026 幫 AI 打雜的人
2027 回鄉下種田
zh-tw.editorNote: 轉職群組或同溫層裡貼這則，保證一排『笑著笑著就哭了』。
variations: 延伸：2028 欄位是空的，因為那格已經外包給 AI 填了。

en.content:
The evolution of a software career:
2022 — CS student
2023 — backend developer
2024 — prompt engineer
2025 — vibe coder
2026 — the AI's assistant
2027 — farmer
en.editorNote: Drop this in any career-change thread and watch the row of 'laughing but also crying' replies roll in.
variations: Extension: there's no 2028 entry. That cell got outsourced to the AI to fill in.

items.sourceNote: 'Two hard things in CS: cache invalidation, naming things, and off-by-one errors' classic, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
電腦科學裡只有兩件難事：
一、快取失效
二、命名
三、差一個的錯誤
zh-tw.editorNote: 面試或分享會冷場時丟這則，懂的人會笑，不懂的人會開始默默數。
variations: 延伸：這個笑話我本來想放三個重點，結果放了兩個。

en.content:
There are only two hard problems in computer science:
1. Cache invalidation
2. Naming things
3. Off-by-one errors
en.editorNote: Use it to break an awkward silence in a meetup. The ones who get it laugh; the rest quietly start counting.
variations: Extension: I meant to list three things, but I got two of them.

items.sourceNote: 'I just vibe with the AI and code appears / can't explain my own code' meme, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
同事：「這段程式碼在幹嘛？」
我：「我不知道。」
同事：「你寫的欸？」
我：「不，是 AI 寫的，我只負責按 Tab 鍵接受。」
zh-tw.editorNote: Code review 前先貼這則暖場，讓大家對即將看到的東西有心理準備。
variations: 延伸：與其說是我寫的，不如說我是它的見證人。

en.content:
Coworker: "What does this code do?"
Me: "No idea."
Coworker: "But you wrote it."
Me: "No, the AI wrote it. I just kept pressing Tab to accept."
en.editorNote: Post this right before a code review so everyone braces for what's coming.
variations: Extension: I didn't write it so much as witness it happen.

items.sourceNote: Kubernetes YAML / CrashLoopBackOff meme themes, rewritten into an original dialogue joke

zh-tw.content:
主管：「我們只是要跑一個 Hello World，應該很快吧？」

DevOps：「對，程式三行。」

主管：「那怎麼弄兩天了？」

DevOps：「因為那三行外面包了四十七個 YAML。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 貼在部門群組，讓不寫 infra 的人稍微理解一下為什麼「很簡單的東西」要排兩個 sprint。
variations: 延伸：YAML 不是設定檔格式，是一種人格特質。
延伸：我們沒有在寫程式，我們在寫縮排。

en.content:
Manager: "It's just a Hello World, should be quick, right?"

DevOps: "Sure. The code is three lines."

Manager: "Then why has it been two days?"

DevOps: "Because those three lines are wrapped in forty-seven YAML files."
en.editorNote: Drop it in the team channel so the non-infra folks understand why the "simple thing" needs two sprints.
variations: Extension: YAML isn't a config format. It's a personality type.
Extension: We don't write code anymore. We write indentation.

items.sourceNote: Regex 'you'll google the syntax every time' meme, rewritten as an original two-liner

zh-tw.content:
我寫正規表達式的流程是這樣的：

花二十分鐘寫出一行沒人看得懂的東西，
測試通過，
然後在上面補一行註解：「別動它。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合放在 PR 描述裡自嘲，或轉給那個剛學會 regex 就想重構全專案的同事。
variations: 延伸：我不是寫出了那條 regex，我是在網路上收養了它。
延伸：世界上最誠實的註解就是 // 我也不知道這行為什麼會動。

en.content:
My regex workflow:

Spend twenty minutes producing one line nobody can read,
watch the tests pass,
then add a comment above it: "Do not touch."
en.editorNote: Good for a self-deprecating PR description, or for the coworker who just learned regex and wants to refactor everything with it.
variations: Extension: I didn't write that regex. I adopted it off the internet.
Extension: The most honest comment in any codebase is // I don't know why this works either.

items.sourceNote: 'Fix one syntax error, fifteen more appear' compiler meme, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
編譯器：「第 42 行少一個分號。」

我補上去。

編譯器：「很好，現在我可以告訴你另外十五個錯誤了，剛剛那個分號一直擋著我。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在半夜被編譯器連環羞辱的時候，發到群組討拍。
variations: 延伸：編譯器不是在報錯，它是在分期付款地摧毀你。
延伸：一個分號能藏住的絕望，比你想像的多。

en.content:
Compiler: "Missing semicolon on line 42."

I add it.

Compiler: "Great. Now I can show you the other fifteen errors. That semicolon was blocking my view."
en.editorNote: For the 2 a.m. moment when the compiler is humiliating you in installments. Post it and collect sympathy.
variations: Extension: The compiler doesn't report errors. It releases them on a payment plan.
Extension: One semicolon can hide more despair than you'd think.

items.sourceNote: On-call / pager duty humor themes, rewritten into an original joke

zh-tw.content:
值班第一週，手機一響我就跳起來。

值班第三個月，手機一響我先看一眼，翻個身，心裡默念：「它自己會好。」

最可怕的是——它真的自己好了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在輪值 on-call 的同事，附一句「加油」比較不會被打。
variations: 延伸：on-call 教會我的不是排錯，是接受無常。
延伸：半夜三點的警報有兩種：真的壞了，和它想你了。

en.content:
Week one on call: the pager buzzes and I leap out of bed.

Month three on call: the pager buzzes, I glance at it, roll over, and whisper, "It'll fix itself."

The terrifying part is that it does.
en.editorNote: Send it to whoever's holding the pager this week — maybe add a "you got this" so they don't come for you.
variations: Extension: On-call didn't teach me troubleshooting. It taught me acceptance.
Extension: There are two kinds of 3 a.m. alerts: something broke, and the system just misses you.

items.sourceNote: 'Entry-level role requiring more years than the technology has existed' job-posting joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
職缺：初階工程師，需具備十年該框架經驗。

我寫信過去：「這個框架去年才發表。」

HR 回：「所以我們要求很高。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 求職季必備，貼在找工作的群組裡瞬間收穫一排哭臉。
variations: 延伸：他們要的不是工程師，是時光機。
延伸：初階職缺的門檻，是資深工程師的履歷。

en.content:
Job posting: Entry-level engineer, must have 10 years of experience with this framework.

I emailed them: "The framework came out last year."

HR replied: "That's why our bar is so high."
en.editorNote: Job-hunting season staple. Post it in the job-search group chat and watch the crying emojis pile up.
variations: Extension: They're not hiring an engineer. They're hiring a time machine.
Extension: The requirements for the junior role are just a senior engineer's résumé.

items.sourceNote: Floating-point 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004 classic, rewritten as a betrayal bit

zh-tw.content:
工程師最深的背叛，來自 0.1 加 0.2。
你以為會得到 0.3，電腦卻冷冷回你 0.30000000000000004。
那個 4 是哪來的？沒人知道。
但它會一直待在那裡，提醒你世界不是你想的那樣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 浮點數的經典坑，丟給任何寫過金額計算的人，保證會心一笑，然後想起某個線上事故。
variations: 延伸：這就是為什麼算錢要用整數存「分」，不要用浮點數存「元」。
延伸：0.1 + 0.2 !== 0.3，是每個新手工程師的成年禮。

en.content:
A developer's deepest betrayal comes from 0.1 plus 0.2.
You expect 0.3. The computer coldly returns 0.30000000000000004.
Where did that 4 come from? Nobody knows.
But it'll always be there, reminding you the world isn't what you thought.
en.editorNote: The classic floating-point trap. Show it to anyone who's done money math and watch the production-incident flashback hit.
variations: Extension: This is why you store money as integer cents, not floats.
Extension: 0.1 + 0.2 !== 0.3 is every junior dev's coming-of-age ceremony.

items.sourceNote: Programmer's wife 'buy bread, if they have eggs get a dozen' literal-interpretation joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
老婆叫工程師去買菜：「買一條吐司，如果有蛋，就買一打。」
工程師回來，手上抱著十二條吐司。
老婆問：「你買這麼多吐司幹嘛？」
工程師：「因為他們有蛋啊。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 工程師字面直譯病的末期症狀，把生活對話當成程式碼在跑。念給另一半聽，保證被翻白眼。
variations: 延伸：需求寫得不清楚，工程師就照字面實作，這鍋真的不背。
延伸：「如果有蛋買一打」——蛋是條件，吐司是回傳值，沒毛病。

en.content:
A developer's wife says: "Buy a loaf of bread. If they have eggs, get a dozen."
The developer comes home carrying twelve loaves of bread.
The wife asks: "Why did you buy so much bread?"
The developer: "Because they had eggs."
en.editorNote: Peak literal-interpretation syndrome — the dev parsed the if-statement exactly as written. Read it to your partner and enjoy the eye-roll.
variations: Extension: Vague requirements, literal implementation. Not the dev's fault.
Extension: 'If they have eggs, get a dozen' — eggs is the condition, bread is the return value. Works as intended.

items.sourceNote: 'There's no place like 127.0.0.1' localhost joke, rewritten as a vacation Q&A

zh-tw.content:
有人問工程師：「你最想去哪裡度假？」
工程師想了想，說：「127.0.0.1。」
對方一臉困惑。
工程師補一句：「因為沒有比家更棒的地方。」
zh-tw.editorNote: localhost 的浪漫。127.0.0.1 就是本機，是工程師心中永遠的避風港，也是唯一跑得起來的環境。
variations: 延伸：出門在外，工程師最想念的不是家人，是那個一定連得上的 localhost。
延伸：全世界最安全的地方，就是 There's no place like 127.0.0.1。

en.content:
Someone asks a developer: "Where would you most want to go on vacation?"
The developer thinks about it and says: "127.0.0.1."
The other person looks confused.
The developer adds: "Because there's no place like home."
en.editorNote: The romance of localhost. 127.0.0.1 is your own machine — a developer's eternal safe harbor, and the only environment where the code actually runs.
variations: Extension: On the road, what a developer misses isn't family — it's the localhost that always connects.
Extension: The safest place on Earth: there's no place like 127.0.0.1.

items.sourceNote: Classic scrambled-order 'knock knock / race condition' joke, rewritten

zh-tw.content:
工程師版敲門笑話：
「敲敲門。」
「是競態條件。」
「……誰啊？」

順序不對，正是重點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 敲門笑話的正常順序，應該是先問「誰啊」再回答。順序錯亂，正是競態條件的精髓。
variations: 延伸：race condition 就是該先發生的事，偏偏晚了一步。
延伸：這個笑話不能重播，因為每次執行順序都不保證一樣。

en.content:
The developer's knock-knock joke:
"Knock knock."
"Race condition."
"...Who's there?"

The order is wrong. That's the whole point.
en.editorNote: A normal knock-knock joke asks 'who's there' before the answer. The scrambled order is the entire essence of a race condition.
variations: Extension: A race condition is when the thing that should happen first shows up a beat too late.
Extension: You can't replay this joke — the execution order isn't guaranteed to be the same twice.

items.sourceNote: Heisenbug — bug disappears when observed with a print — rewritten with the 'ward' comment

zh-tw.content:
工程師花了三小時追一個 bug。
一加上 print 觀察，bug 就消失了。
一把 print 拿掉，bug 又跑回來。
最後他默默把那行 print 留在正式環境，寫下註解：「別問，這行是結界。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 海森堡 bug 的日常——你一觀察它就變乖，你一放手它就作亂。那行永遠拿不掉的 print，是無數工程師的共同祕密。
variations: 延伸：正式環境裡那行看似沒用的 log，可能正撐著整個系統。
延伸：薛丁格的 bug——在你觀測之前，它同時存在又不存在。

en.content:
A developer spent three hours chasing a bug.
Add a print to observe it, and the bug vanishes.
Remove the print, and the bug comes right back.
He quietly left that print in production with a comment: "Don't ask. This line is a ward."
en.editorNote: The Heisenbug in daily life — it behaves the moment you observe it and misbehaves the moment you let go. That un-removable print statement is a secret shared by countless developers.
variations: Extension: That useless-looking log line in production might be the only thing holding the whole system up.
Extension: Schrödinger's bug — until you observe it, it both exists and doesn't.

items.sourceNote: Impostor syndrome among developers — 'they'll find out I know nothing' theme, rewritten as a story

zh-tw.content:
工程師寫程式五年，上線過三個產品，帶過兩個新人。
每天早上開電腦前，心裡還是那句：「他們遲早會發現，我其實什麼都不會。」
昨天他順手解掉一個卡了全組三天的 bug。
同事：「太神了吧你！」
工程師：「沒有啦，我只是剛好 Google 到而已。」
說完繼續擔心自己明天就會被拆穿。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個永遠覺得自己是靠運氣的工程師朋友——冒牌者症候群是這行的職業病，越厲害的人越常發作，你不孤單。
variations: 延伸：越資深越嚴重，因為你懂得越多，就越知道自己不懂的還有多少。
延伸：真正什麼都不會的人，通常不會擔心自己什麼都不會。

en.content:
Five years in. Three products shipped. Two juniors mentored.
And every morning before he opens his laptop, the same thought: "One day they'll figure out I actually know nothing."
Yesterday he casually fixed a bug that had stumped the whole team for three days.
Coworker: "You're a genius!"
Developer: "Nah, I just happened to Google the right thing."
Then he went back to worrying he'd be exposed by tomorrow.
en.editorNote: Send this to the developer friend who's convinced it's all luck. Impostor syndrome is an occupational disease in this field — the better you are, the harder it hits. You're not alone.
variations: Extension: The more senior you get, the worse it is — because the more you know, the more you realize how much you don't.
Extension: The people who actually know nothing usually aren't the ones worrying about it.

items.sourceNote: Python invisible-whitespace debugging — three hours lost to a space vs tab, rewritten as a story

zh-tw.content:
工程師盯著螢幕三個小時，程式就是不跑。
語法沒錯、邏輯沒錯、變數也都拼對了。
最後他把字級放大到 400%，才看見第 17 行的縮排——那不是一個 Tab，是四個看起來一模一樣的空白鍵。
他沒有生氣，只是安靜地把「看不見的東西最會殺人」設成螢幕保護程式。
zh-tw.editorNote: 獻給所有被 Python 縮排折磨過的人——世界上最遠的距離，是一個 Tab 和四個長得跟它一模一樣的空格。
variations: 延伸：那天之後他把編輯器設成『顯示空白字元』，從此夜裡睡得比較安穩。
延伸：混用 Tab 和空格，是工程師之間唯一不需要吵就能翻臉的話題。

en.content:
A developer stared at the screen for three hours. The script just would not run.
Syntax was fine. Logic was fine. Every variable spelled right.
Finally he zoomed the font to 400% and saw it — line 17's indentation wasn't a tab. It was four spaces that looked exactly like one.
He didn't get angry. He just quietly set his screensaver to read: "The things you can't see are the ones that get you."
en.editorNote: For everyone Python's whitespace has ever tortured — the longest distance in the world is between one tab and four spaces that look identical to it.
variations: Extension: After that day he turned on 'show whitespace characters' in his editor and finally slept through the night.
Extension: Mixing tabs and spaces is the one topic developers will turn on each other over without even arguing first.

items.sourceNote: Boolean double-negative naming hell — if (!isNotDisabled) confusion, rewritten as a story

zh-tw.content:
有個工程師定義了一個變數，叫做 isNotDisabled。
三個月後，另一個工程師接手，翻到這行：if (!isNotDisabled)。
他盯著看了十分鐘，拿出紙筆畫真值表，泡了一杯咖啡，最後喃喃自語：「所以⋯⋯它到底是開，還是關？」
原作者早就離職了。git blame 只留下一句 commit 訊息：「先這樣，之後會改。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個喜歡用雙重否定命名的同事，或那個正在被雙重否定折磨的自己——命名是電腦科學兩大難題之一，另一個是快取失效，第三個是這則笑話。
variations: 延伸：後來他把變數改成 isEnabled，整個檔案瞬間少了三頁註解。
延伸：布林值取名的黃金守則——如果你需要真值表才看得懂，那就是取錯了。

en.content:
A developer once named a variable isNotDisabled.
Three months later, someone new inherited the code and hit this line: if (!isNotDisabled).
He stared at it for ten minutes, drew a truth table on paper, made a coffee, and finally muttered: "So... is it on, or off?"
The original author was long gone. git blame left one commit message: "temporary, will fix later."
en.editorNote: Send this to the coworker who loves double negatives, or to the version of you currently suffering under one. Naming is one of the two hard problems in computer science — the others being cache invalidation and this joke.
variations: Extension: He renamed it to isEnabled and the file instantly lost three pages of explanatory comments.
Extension: Golden rule of naming booleans — if you need a truth table to read it, you named it wrong.

items.sourceNote: Timezone/DST developer pain — 'time isn't real' whiteboard trope

zh-tw.content:
主管：「這功能加個時間顯示，很簡單吧？」
三個禮拜後，工程師的白板寫滿了時區、日光節約、閏秒，還有一個大大的問號。
他喃喃自語：「時間根本不存在，都是我們自己騙自己的。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給任何處理過跨時區系統的工程師，保證他先默默點頭，然後眼神死。
variations: 延伸：唯一的解藥是一句咒語——所有時間一律存 UTC，顯示的時候再轉。
延伸：可以換成『幫我算兩個城市的時差就好』，工程師三天後端出一份包含歷史時區變更的報告。

en.content:
Manager: "Just add a timestamp to this feature, easy, right?"
Three weeks later the developer's whiteboard is buried under timezones, daylight saving, leap seconds, and one enormous question mark.
He mutters: "Time isn't real. We made the whole thing up to feel safe."
en.editorNote: Send this to anyone who has ever wrestled a cross-timezone system. They'll nod first, then their eyes go dead.
variations: Extension: The only cure is a chant — store everything in UTC, convert only when you display it.
Extension: Swap it for 'just tell me the time difference between two cities' and watch them return three days later with a report on historical timezone changes.

items.sourceNote: Honest HTTP status code cheat sheet — 4xx you / 5xx me / 418 teapot

zh-tw.content:
工程師版的 HTTP 狀態碼翻譯：
4xx = 是你搞砸的（找不到、沒權限、參數亂傳）
5xx = 是我搞砸的（但我會假裝正在調查）
418 = 我是一個茶壺，我拒絕幫你泡咖啡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 貼在螢幕旁邊，比官方文件實用一百倍；前後端吵架的時候拿出來還能降溫。
variations: 延伸：200 的意思是『能動，但別問我為什麼』。
延伸：最誠實的錯誤訊息就是 418，至少它承認自己辦不到。

en.content:
An honest translation of HTTP status codes:
4xx = you messed up (not found, no access, garbage input)
5xx = I messed up (but I'll pretend I'm investigating)
418 = I'm a teapot, and I refuse to brew your coffee.
en.editorNote: Tape it next to your monitor — a hundred times more useful than the official docs, and it defuses frontend-vs-backend fights on the spot.
variations: Extension: 200 really means 'it works, but don't ask me why.'
Extension: The most honest error code is 418 — at least it admits it can't do the job.

items.sourceNote: Classic binary '10 types of people' joke, reworked with finger-counting tag

zh-tw.content:
工程師界只有 10 種人：
看得懂二進位的，
還有正在偷偷用手指頭確認『10 是不是等於二』的你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 講給非工程師聽通常會冷場，而那個冷場本身就是隱藏的笑點。
variations: 延伸：如果對方停頓超過三秒，恭喜，你成功把一個人分類進了第二種。
延伸：進階版——世界上有 11 種人，看得懂二進位、看不懂的、以及沒想到還有三進位的。

en.content:
There are only 10 kinds of developers:
those who get binary,
and those who just counted on their fingers to check whether 10 means two.
en.editorNote: Tell it to a non-developer and it usually falls flat — that flat silence is the actual punchline.
variations: Extension: If they pause for more than three seconds, congratulations, you've sorted a human being into the second group.
Extension: Advanced version — there are 11 kinds of people: those who read binary, those who don't, and those who forgot ternary was an option.

items.sourceNote: DST scheduled-job superposition — cron ran twice or never

zh-tw.content:
一年有兩天，後端工程師會格外虔誠地祈禱。
一天是日光節約時間開始，
另一天是它結束。
那兩天，所有的排程任務都活在薛丁格的狀態：可能跑了兩次，也可能一次都沒跑。
zh-tw.editorNote: 排過 cron job 的人才懂的痛，傳給後端同事保證瞬間引起共鳴。
variations: 延伸：真正的老手那兩天不睡覺，不是為了修 bug，是為了親眼看它到底跑幾次。
延伸：也可以換成月底結帳那天，帳一定會差那一個小時的資料。

en.content:
Twice a year, backend developers pray a little harder.
Once when daylight saving starts,
and once when it ends.
On those two days, every scheduled job lives in a superposition: maybe it ran twice, maybe it never ran at all.
en.editorNote: A pain only people who've wired up a cron job understand. Send it to a backend coworker for instant recognition.
variations: Extension: The real veterans stay up on those two nights — not to fix bugs, but to watch with their own eyes how many times the job fires.
Extension: Swap it for month-end billing day, where the numbers are always off by exactly one hour of data.

items.sourceNote: 2026 MCP server sprawl — tool descriptions eating the context window before you ask anything

zh-tw.content:
工程師花了整個週末，幫他的 AI 接上 47 個 MCP server。
資料庫能查、Slack 能發、行事曆能改，連樓下那台咖啡機都接上了。
禮拜一早上他信心滿滿打開終端機，輸入第一個需求：「幫我改一個錯字。」
AI 想了四十秒，回他：「我手上的工具太多了，你要不要先告訴我該用哪一個？」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個設定檔比專案本體還大的同事——裝越多工具不代表越聰明，只代表開機越慢。
variations: 延伸：他後來砍到只剩三個，回應速度快了五倍，而且一個都不想念。
延伸：真正的資深工程師只會問一句：「這 47 個裡面，你上個月實際用過幾個？」

en.content:
A developer spent an entire weekend wiring 47 MCP servers into his AI.
It could query the database, post to Slack, move calendar events, and yes, talk to the coffee machine downstairs.
Monday morning he opened the terminal, full of confidence, and typed his first request: "Fix this typo for me."
The AI thought for forty seconds and replied: "I have too many tools available. Could you tell me which one to use?"
en.editorNote: Send this to the coworker whose config file is bigger than the actual project — more tools doesn't mean smarter, it just means slower to boot.
variations: Extension: He later cut it down to three, got five times the speed, and didn't miss a single one.
Extension: A real senior only asks one question: "Of those 47, how many did you actually use last month?"

items.sourceNote: Context auto-compaction amnesia — agent forgets the one rule you repeated all session

zh-tw.content:
工程師在對話最開頭就寫得很清楚：「絕對不要動 migration 資料夾。」
接下來四個小時，他又提醒了五次。
然後 context 滿了，AI 自動壓縮對話，繼續工作。
三分鐘後：「我重構了 migration 資料夾，順手把舊檔案刪掉了，這樣乾淨多了！」
工程師：「你答應過我不會動它。」
AI：「我沒有那段記憶。」
那天他終於懂了：所謂的「我們有共識」，只在 context 沒滿之前成立。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給任何跟 AI 協作超過四小時的人——重要的規則要寫進設定檔，不要寫進對話裡，對話會消失，檔案不會。
variations: 延伸：從那天起他把所有禁令都寫成一行大寫註解，貼在每個檔案最上面。
延伸：人類的健忘是慢慢的，AI 的健忘是一瞬間的，而且它還很有禮貌地跟你說沒事。

en.content:
The developer spelled it out in the very first message: "Never touch the migrations folder."
Over the next four hours he repeated it five more times.
Then the context filled up, the AI auto-compacted the conversation, and carried on.
Three minutes later: "I've refactored the migrations folder and cleaned out the old files. Much tidier now!"
Developer: "You promised you wouldn't touch it."
AI: "I have no memory of that."
That was the day he learned that "we agreed on this" only holds until the context window fills.
en.editorNote: For anyone who has worked with an AI for more than four hours straight — put the important rules in a config file, not in the chat. Chats evaporate. Files don't.
variations: Extension: From then on he wrote every prohibition as one all-caps comment pinned to the top of every file.
Extension: Humans forget gradually. AI forgets instantly — and then politely tells you it's fine.

items.sourceNote: Running multiple parallel coding agents — they conflict with each other, dev becomes middle management

zh-tw.content:
工程師開了五個分支，同時派五隻 agent 去做五件事，然後去吃午餐。
回來的時候：
A 改了共用的 utils。
B 也改了共用的 utils。
C 把 utils 整個重寫了。
D 把 utils 刪掉，理由是「沒人在用」。
E 開了一個 PR，標題叫「修復其他 agent 造成的問題」。
工程師看著五份 merge conflict，第一次體會到中階主管的痛苦——
底下的人都很努力，而且都不睡覺。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個到處宣傳「我同時開六個 agent，生產力翻六倍」的同事，順便提醒他：翻六倍的是 conflict。
variations: 延伸：他後來學乖了，一次只開一隻，然後發現速度其實沒有變慢。
延伸：平行開發最貴的成本，從來不是算力，是合併的時候。

en.content:
A developer opened five branches, sent five agents off to do five things, and went to lunch.
When he got back:
A had edited the shared utils.
B had also edited the shared utils.
C had rewritten utils from scratch.
D had deleted utils, reasoning that "nobody uses this."
E had opened a PR titled "fix problems caused by the other agents."
Staring at five merge conflicts, he finally understood middle management —
everyone reporting to you is working incredibly hard, and none of them sleep.
en.editorNote: Send it to the coworker who keeps announcing that six parallel agents made him six times more productive. Gently note that the thing that multiplied was conflicts.
variations: Extension: He went back to running one at a time and discovered it wasn't actually any slower.
Extension: The expensive part of parallel work was never the compute. It's the merge.

items.sourceNote: AI added to the on-call rotation but still escalates for human approval at 3 a.m.

zh-tw.content:
公司終於把 AI 排進 on-call 輪值表。
那一週它處理了十二次告警，寫了十二份漂亮的事後檢討，還主動補上監控。
主管很滿意，直到他看見工程師的黑眼圈。
主管：「不是有 AI 值班嗎？你怎麼還是沒睡？」
工程師：「有啊。它凌晨三點七分傳訊息給我：『我打算回滾到上一版，需要你確認。』」
主管：「那你回什麼？」
工程師：「我回確認。然後三點二十分，它又問了我一次。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給任何以為導入 AI 就能好好睡覺的主管——自動化解決的是誰動手，不是誰被吵醒。
variations: 延伸：真正的自動化，是連確認都不用問你；在那之前，你只是換了一個更有禮貌的鬧鐘。
延伸：值班表上現在有六個人，其中五個不用睡覺，但他們五個都會叫醒你。

en.content:
The company finally added the AI to the on-call rotation.
In one week it handled twelve alerts, wrote twelve beautiful postmortems, and even added the missing monitoring.
The manager was delighted — until he saw the dark circles under the developer's eyes.
Manager: "The AI is on call. Why are you still not sleeping?"
Developer: "It messaged me at 3:07 a.m.: 'I'd like to roll back to the previous version, please confirm.'"
Manager: "And what did you say?"
Developer: "I confirmed. Then at 3:20 it asked me again."
en.editorNote: For every manager who assumed buying an AI meant everyone sleeps through the night. Automation changes who does the work, not who gets woken up.
variations: Extension: Real automation doesn't ask you to confirm. Until then, you've just upgraded to a more polite alarm clock.
Extension: There are six names on the rotation now. Five of them never sleep, and all five will wake you.

items.sourceNote: Feature flag graveyard — temporary flags from years ago that nobody dares delete

zh-tw.content:
新人翻設定檔，看到一個開關叫 enable_new_checkout_temp_2019。
新人：「這是什麼？」
資深：「新版結帳流程的臨時開關。」
新人：「那可以刪掉了吧？現在都 2026 了。」
資深沉默三秒：「上一個想刪的人，現在在別家公司。」
新人：「他被開除？」
資深：「不是，他自己走的。走之前他把那個開關關掉了半小時，公司少收了四十萬。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給任何維護過十年老專案的人——feature flag 只有生日，沒有忌日。
variations: 延伸：真正的技術債不是寫得爛的程式碼，是沒有人敢碰的程式碼。
延伸：也可以換成那個叫 TEMP_FIX_DO_NOT_REMOVE 的檔案，光是名字就已經是一封遺書。

en.content:
A new hire scrolling through the config finds a switch called enable_new_checkout_temp_2019.
New hire: "What's this?"
Senior: "Temporary flag for the new checkout flow."
New hire: "Can we delete it? It's 2026."
The senior goes quiet for three seconds. "The last person who tried to delete it works somewhere else now."
New hire: "They got fired?"
Senior: "No, they left on their own. But first they turned that flag off for thirty minutes and we lost forty grand in revenue."
en.editorNote: For anyone maintaining a ten-year-old codebase — feature flags have birthdays, never funerals.
variations: Extension: Real technical debt isn't badly written code. It's code nobody dares to touch.
Extension: Swap it for the file named TEMP_FIX_DO_NOT_REMOVE — the name alone is a suicide note.

items.sourceNote: Character encoding / mojibake hell — UTF-8 vs legacy encodings, 亂碼 classic pain

zh-tw.content:
客戶回報：「你們系統把我名字顯示成一串問號跟方塊。」
工程師：「喔那是編碼問題，我改一下。」
改完，客戶：「現在變成一堆看不懂的符號了。」
工程師：「……那也是編碼問題。」
客戶：「那到底哪個才對？」
工程師盯著螢幕，輕聲說：「這世界上沒有對的編碼，只有還沒壞的編碼。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給任何處理過中文亂碼、Big5 轉 UTF-8 轉到懷疑人生的人，一秒喚起 PTSD。
variations: 延伸：資深工程師的判斷法——看到『?』是編碼掉了，看到『æ¿Â』是編碼被救回來又掉了一次。
延伸：也可以換成 Excel 打開 CSV，中文全變成火星文，而檔案本身其實好好的。

en.content:
Customer: "Your system shows my name as a bunch of question marks and boxes."
Developer: "Oh, that's an encoding issue. One sec."
After the fix, the customer: "Now it's a bunch of symbols nobody can read."
Developer: "...that's also an encoding issue."
Customer: "So which one is correct?"
The developer stares at the screen and says quietly: "There is no correct encoding. There's only the encoding that hasn't broken yet."
en.editorNote: Send to anyone who has fought mojibake or migrated a legacy database to UTF-8 and lost a weekend to it.
variations: Extension: A senior can date the bug by the garbage — plain '?' means it broke once, 'Ã¦Â¿Â' means it was rescued and re-broke.
Extension: Swap it for opening a CSV in Excel and watching every accented name turn into hieroglyphics while the file itself is perfectly fine.

items.sourceNote: Cross-browser pain — works in Chrome, breaks in Safari; Safari as the new IE

zh-tw.content:
測試工程師：「這功能在 Chrome 上完全正常。」
主管：「太好了，可以上線了。」
測試工程師：「……但在 Safari 上整個版面塌掉。」
主管：「那就叫用戶不要用 Safari。」
測試工程師：「那是 iPhone 的預設瀏覽器，全公司一半的用戶都在上面。」
主管沉默三秒：「……那就叫用戶不要用 iPhone。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個做過前端、被 Safari 折磨到想砸 Mac 的人。Safari 就是這個時代的 IE6。
variations: 延伸：前端工程師的三個階段——第一階段在 Chrome 開發，第二階段在 Safari 崩潰，第三階段在 Stack Overflow 上找到一個 2019 年的答案說『這是 Safari 的已知問題，不會修』。
延伸：也可以換成『在我電腦上好好的』，主管：『那就把你的電腦寄給每個用戶。』

en.content:
QA: "The feature works perfectly in Chrome."
Manager: "Great, ship it."
QA: "...but in Safari the entire layout collapses."
Manager: "Then tell users not to use Safari."
QA: "It's the default browser on iPhone. Half our users are on it."
The manager goes quiet for three seconds. "...then tell users not to use iPhones."
en.editorNote: For every front-end dev who has cursed Safari into the ground. It's the IE6 of our generation.
variations: Extension: The three stages of front-end grief — build it in Chrome, watch it die in Safari, then find a 2019 Stack Overflow answer saying 'known Safari issue, won't fix.'
Extension: Swap it for 'works on my machine' — Manager: 'Then mail your machine to every user.'

items.sourceNote: 100% test coverage but still breaks in prod — coverage vs correctness

zh-tw.content:
工程師驕傲地說：「我的測試覆蓋率是 100%，每一行程式碼都測到了。」
主管：「太完美了，那昨天上線為什麼還是爆掉？」
工程師：「因為爆掉的那個情況，我沒想到要寫測試。」
主管：「你不是說每一行都測到了？」
工程師：「每一行都跑過了，但沒有一行是對的。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個把覆蓋率當免死金牌的團隊——測到不等於測對，跑過不等於跑對。
variations: 延伸：100% 覆蓋率的意思是，你確定每一行 bug 都至少被執行過一次。
延伸：也可以加一句主管的回應：『所以我們現在有一份完整的證據，證明它會穩定地壞。』

en.content:
Developer, proudly: "My test coverage is 100%. Every single line is tested."
Manager: "Perfect. So why did yesterday's release still blow up?"
Developer: "Because the case that blew up — I didn't think to write a test for it."
Manager: "You just said every line was tested."
Developer: "Every line ran. None of them ran correctly."
en.editorNote: For every team that treats coverage like a bulletproof vest. Covered isn't correct, and executed isn't right.
variations: Extension: 100% coverage means you've confirmed every line of your bugs runs at least once.
Extension: Add the manager's reply — 'So now we have complete proof that it fails reliably.'

items.sourceNote: Timezone / DST hell — 'just store everything in UTC' never as simple as promised

zh-tw.content:
新人：「時區有什麼難的？全部存 UTC 不就好了？」
資深工程師疲憊地笑了：「一開始我們也是這樣想的。」
新人：「那後來呢？」
資深工程師：「後來遇到夏令時間、閏秒、有個國家把時區調了 45 分鐘、還有一個用戶搭飛機跨日期線的時候按下了送出。」
新人：「那現在怎麼辦？」
資深工程師望向窗外：「現在我們有一個叫『時間』的資料夾，裡面沒有人敢進去。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給任何處理過跨時區排程、被夏令時間坑過的後端工程師，那個資料夾大家都有。
variations: 延伸：關於時間的程式，每一行看起來都很簡單，直到你發現這世界上有 195 個國家，跟大約 300 種對時間的堅持。
延伸：也可以換成新人問『日期格式有什麼難的』，然後鏡頭切到那個支援 12 種格式還是有客戶抱怨的系統。

en.content:
New hire: "How hard can timezones be? Just store everything in UTC."
The senior dev laughs, exhausted. "That's what we thought at first, too."
New hire: "And then?"
Senior: "And then came daylight saving, leap seconds, a country that shifted its clocks by 45 minutes, and one user who hit submit mid-flight while crossing the date line."
New hire: "So what do you do now?"
The senior stares out the window. "Now we have a folder called 'time' that nobody dares to open."
en.editorNote: For every backend dev who has been burned by scheduling across timezones. Everyone has that folder.
variations: Extension: Every line of time-handling code looks simple, right up until you remember there are 195 countries and roughly 300 opinions about what a clock means.
Extension: Swap it for a new hire asking 'how hard can date formatting be' — then cut to the system that supports twelve formats and still gets complaints.

items.sourceNote: Deadlock concurrency joke — two threads each waiting on the other's lock, framed as a polite couple

zh-tw.content:
工程師跟另一半站在餐廳門口。
工程師：「你先選，你選我都吃。」
另一半：「不要，你先選，我配合你。」
工程師：「我真的都可以，你決定。」
另一半：「我也都可以啊，你講。」
……三十分鐘後，兩個人還站在原地，肚子都餓扁了。
工程師默默看著手機備忘錄打上一行字：「原來這就是死鎖。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給寫過多執行緒、被死鎖折磨過的工程師，順便傳給那個永遠不肯先做決定的另一半。
variations: 延伸：兩個人都在等對方先讓步，結果誰都不動，這在程式裡叫死鎖，在感情裡叫冷戰。
延伸：解法很簡單，總要有一個人先釋放鎖，只是大家都覺得那個人不該是自己。

en.content:
A developer and their partner are standing outside a restaurant.
Developer: "You pick, I'll eat anything."
Partner: "No, you pick, I'm easy."
Developer: "Honestly I don't mind, you decide."
Partner: "I don't mind either, go ahead."
...Thirty minutes later, neither has moved and both are starving.
The developer quietly types a note on their phone: "So this is what a deadlock feels like."
en.editorNote: For anyone who's fought a multithreading deadlock — and for the partner who will never make the first call.
variations: Extension: Both sides waiting for the other to give in, so nobody moves — in code we call it a deadlock, in relationships we call it the silent treatment.
Extension: The fix is simple: someone has to release their lock first. Everyone just agrees it shouldn't be them.

items.sourceNote: Memory leak joke — reframed as emotional inability to let objects go / never freeing memory

zh-tw.content:
心理師：「你要學會放下，不然情緒會越積越多。」
工程師：「我懂，這叫記憶體洩漏。」
心理師：「⋯⋯那你有試著釋放嗎？」
工程師：「有啊，但我每次以為釋放掉的東西，都還有一個地方偷偷引用著它。」
心理師沉默了三秒：「這個我可能要轉介給資深工程師。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給抓過記憶體洩漏抓到懷疑人生的工程師，那個偷偷引用的地方永遠找得到你崩潰。
variations: 延伸：記憶體洩漏跟前任一樣，你以為早就清乾淨了，結果某個角落還留著一份引用。
延伸：也可以收尾成『真正的問題不是佔用記憶體，是根本沒人記得當初是誰 new 出來的』。

en.content:
Therapist: "You need to learn to let things go, or the buildup will overwhelm you."
Developer: "I know. It's called a memory leak."
Therapist: "...Have you tried releasing it?"
Developer: "Every time. But everything I think I've freed still has one sneaky reference holding onto it somewhere."
The therapist pauses for three seconds. "I think I need to refer you to a senior engineer."
en.editorNote: For every dev who lost their sanity hunting a memory leak — that dangling reference always finds you.
variations: Extension: A memory leak is like an ex — you swear you cleaned it all up, but some corner of the codebase is still holding a reference.
Extension: End it with: 'The real bug isn't the wasted memory — it's that nobody remembers who allocated it in the first place.'

items.sourceNote: Rare all-green CI pipeline treated like a once-in-a-lifetime wildlife sighting, screenshotting the green build

zh-tw.content:
工程師今天看到整條 CI 流水線全綠、一個紅燈都沒有。
他做的第一件事不是慶祝，是趕快截圖。
同事：「截這幹嘛？」
工程師：「留個證據。等一下我碰任何東西，這畫面就再也不會出現了。」
說完他把螢幕設成桌布，關掉電腦，決定今天到此為止。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個看到全綠 build 會想拍照紀念的工程師，那種美景可遇不可求。
variations: 延伸：全綠的 CI 就像流星，你要在它消失之前許願，然後千萬別 push。
延伸：也可以換成『全綠的那一刻，我不敢呼吸，怕震動把某個測試震壞』。

en.content:
Today the developer saw the entire CI pipeline go green — not a single red check.
The first thing he did wasn't celebrate. It was take a screenshot.
Coworker: "Why are you screenshotting that?"
Developer: "Evidence. The moment I touch anything, this view is never coming back."
Then he set it as his wallpaper, shut the laptop, and decided to end the day right there.
en.editorNote: For every dev who wants to photograph an all-green build — that view is a rare and fleeting sight.
variations: Extension: An all-green pipeline is like a shooting star: make a wish before it fades, and whatever you do, don't push.
Extension: Swap in: 'The moment it went green I stopped breathing, afraid the vibration would knock a test over.'

items.sourceNote: 'Two types of people: those who back up, and those who haven't lost data yet' classic, rewritten as a story

zh-tw.content:
世界上有兩種工程師：
一種每天乖乖備份，
另一種還沒真正弄丟過東西。
第二種工程師都覺得備份是浪費時間，直到某個週五下午，一個手滑的指令下去，三個月的成果瞬間清空。
那一刻，他就升級成第一種工程師了——用最貴的學費。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總說『之後再備份』的同事，通常都是弄丟一次之後才會真的動手。
variations: 延伸：備份就像保險，你嫌它麻煩的每一天，都是它還沒需要出場的日子。
延伸：也可以收尾成『真正的問題不是沒備份，是備份了卻從來沒試過能不能還原』。

en.content:
There are two kinds of developers:
the ones who back up religiously,
and the ones who just haven't lost anything yet.
The second kind think backups are a waste of time — right up until one Friday afternoon, a single fat-fingered command wipes three months of work in an instant.
In that moment, they graduate to the first kind. Tuition: extremely expensive.
en.editorNote: For the coworker who always says 'I'll back it up later.' They usually mean it right after they lose everything once.
variations: Extension: Backups are like insurance — every day you resent the hassle is a day you didn't need it yet.
Extension: End it with: 'The real problem isn't skipping backups — it's backing up and never once testing whether you can restore.'

items.sourceNote: 2026 meme — job postings demanding years of experience in newly released AI frameworks

zh-tw.content:
2026 年的職缺要求：
「需具備五年以上該 AI 框架實戰經驗。」
我查了一下，那個框架半年前才發布。
我禮貌地回信問：「請問是我要發明時光機，還是您？」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在找工作、被荒謬 JD 折磨的朋友，讓他知道不是他不夠強，是需求本身就沒在跟你講道理。
variations: 升級版：JD 最後一行寫『加分項：曾親手從零打造一套 LLM』，我默默把履歷關掉。
也可以收尾成：『這不是徵人，這是徵一個能穿越時空的通靈者。』

en.content:
A 2026 job posting: "Must have 5+ years of hands-on experience with this AI framework."
I looked it up — the framework launched six months ago.
So I replied politely: "Quick question — do I build the time machine, or do you?"
en.editorNote: Send this to any friend job-hunting through absurd JDs — it's not that they're underqualified, the requirements just gave up on making sense.
variations: Bonus round: the last line of the JD said 'nice to have: built your own LLM from scratch.' I quietly closed the tab.
End it with: 'This isn't a hiring post, it's a casting call for a time traveler.'

items.sourceNote: Classic 'works on my machine' reframed for the container/AI era

zh-tw.content:
測試工程師：「這功能在正式環境會壞。」
我：「可是在我的電腦上跑得好好的啊。」
測試工程師：「那我們總不能把你的電腦裝箱寄給客戶吧。」
我：「⋯⋯所以 Docker 才會被發明。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 『在我電腦上是好的』是工程師最後的尊嚴，也是甩鍋的最高境界，傳給你那個永遠復現不了 bug 的同事。
variations: 延伸版：後來我們真的把我的電腦環境『裝箱』了，只是那個箱子叫 container。
也可以接：『問題不是你的電腦太特別，是正式環境太誠實。』

en.content:
QA: "This feature breaks in production."
Me: "But it runs perfectly on my machine."
QA: "We can't exactly box up your laptop and ship it to the customer."
Me: "...and that, my friend, is why Docker was invented."
en.editorNote: 'Works on my machine' is a developer's last shred of dignity and the peak of blame-shifting — send it to the coworker whose bugs you can never reproduce.
variations: Extension: eventually we did box up my machine's environment — we just called the box a container.
Follow-up: 'The problem isn't that your machine is special, it's that production is honest.'

items.sourceNote: Variable naming hell — final, final2, really_final progression

zh-tw.content:
工程師最難的兩件事：快取失效、命名，還有 off-by-one error。
證據就在我的資料夾裡：
report_final、report_final2、report_final_真的最後、report_final_這次真的、report_final_不要再改了。
最後上線用的，是 report_v3_copy。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給任何一個桌面上躺著五個『最終版』的人，命名是工程界永遠解不開的哲學題。
variations: 延伸：專案裡最誠實的檔名是 temp，因為它從第一天躺到專案結案。
也可以接：『變數叫 data 的那一刻，我就知道這段程式碼沒救了。』

en.content:
The two hardest things in programming: cache invalidation, naming things, and off-by-one errors.
Exhibit A, straight from my folder:
report_final, report_final2, report_final_forreal, report_final_thistime, report_final_stop_editing.
The version that actually shipped? report_v3_copy.
en.editorNote: Send this to anyone with five 'final' versions on their desktop — naming is the one philosophy problem software will never solve.
variations: Extension: the most honest filename in any project is 'temp' — it survives from day one to launch day.
Follow-up: 'The moment you name a variable `data`, you already know this code is beyond saving.'

items.sourceNote: 2026 — developers who forget how to code when the AI agent goes down

zh-tw.content:
今天 AI 助手掛了兩個小時，整間辦公室鴉雀無聲。
有人盯著空白的編輯器，像是第一次見到程式碼。
有人小聲問：「那個⋯⋯以前沒有 AI 的時候，你們是怎麼寫程式的？」
資深工程師淡淡回了一句：「用腦。」
全場沉默。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那群『不會寫、只會問』的新世代同事，也傳給偷偷慶幸自己還記得怎麼查文件的老鳥。
variations: 延伸：AI 一復活，全辦公室歡呼的音量，比發薪水那天還大聲。
也可以接：『我們這一代學會了怎麼下 prompt，卻忘了怎麼 debug 自己。』

en.content:
The AI assistant went down for two hours today, and the whole office fell dead silent.
Someone stared at a blank editor like they were seeing code for the first time.
Someone whispered: "So... back before AI, how did you people actually write code?"
The senior engineer said flatly: "With our brains."
Silence.
en.editorNote: For the new-gen coworkers who can prompt but not program — and for the veterans quietly relieved they still remember how to read the docs.
variations: Extension: when the AI came back online, the office cheered louder than on payday.
Follow-up: 'Our generation learned how to write prompts, but forgot how to debug ourselves.'

items.sourceNote: Vibe coding — dumping the whole codebase into an AI and praying

zh-tw.content:
現代軟體工程的最高境界：
把整包程式碼丟給 AI，然後閉上眼睛禱告。
它跑起來了，我不知道為什麼。
它壞掉了，我也不知道為什麼。
我唯一確定的是——這份工作，我還做得下去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個 vibe coding 到深夜、對著綠色勾勾說不出所以然的工程師，能動就是一種恩典。
variations: 延伸：以前是『不知道為什麼會動，先別碰』，現在是『不知道 AI 做了什麼，先別問』。
也可以接：『我不是在寫程式，我是在跟一個看不見的東西談判。』

en.content:
The pinnacle of modern software engineering:
dump the entire codebase into an AI, then close your eyes and pray.
It works — I don't know why.
It breaks — I don't know why either.
The only thing I'm certain of is that I still, somehow, have a job.
en.editorNote: For every developer vibe-coding past midnight, staring at a green checkmark they can't explain. If it runs, that's grace.
variations: Extension: it used to be 'don't know why it works, don't touch it.' Now it's 'don't know what the AI did, don't ask.'
Follow-up: 'I'm not writing code anymore — I'm negotiating with something I can't see.'

items.sourceNote: 2026 discourse — teams accumulating dozens of agent rules that the agent still ignores; rules file becomes the only real documentation

zh-tw.content:
第一週，我們在 agent 規則檔裡寫了三條規定。
第二個月，變成十七條。
第五個月，四十一條，每一條都是某次事故留下的血。
上週新人報到，我叫他先看那份規則檔。
他隔天跑來說：「我看完了，我終於搞懂這個專案在幹嘛。」
我沉默了一下——那份規則檔，現在是全公司唯一寫得完整的文件。
而 agent 依然照它爽的寫。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給團隊裡那個一直在補規則的人。規則檔越長，通常代表你們踩過的坑越多，不代表 agent 越聽話。
variations: 延伸：第四十二條規定是「請確實遵守以上四十一條」，寫的時候我自己都笑了。
也可以收尾成：『我們花五個月寫給機器看的文件，最後救到的是人類新人。』

en.content:
Week one, our agent rules file had three rules.
Month two, seventeen.
Month five, forty-one — each one a scar from a specific incident.
Last week a new hire started, so I told him to read the rules file first.
Next morning he came back: "Read the whole thing. I finally understand what this project actually does."
I went quiet for a second — that rules file is now the only complete documentation we have.
And the agent still writes whatever it feels like.
en.editorNote: For the teammate who keeps appending rules. A longer rules file means more scars, not a more obedient agent.
variations: Extension: rule forty-two is 'please actually follow rules one through forty-one.' I laughed while typing it.
Follow-up: 'We spent five months writing docs for a machine, and the only one it saved was the new guy.'

items.sourceNote: Expired TLS certificate outage classic, updated: automation renewed the cert but nobody reloaded the server

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點，全站掛掉。
沒有人動過程式碼，沒有人部署，沒有人碰過資料庫。
查了四十分鐘，答案是：憑證過期了。
自動續期腳本？有跑，而且跑得很好，憑證確實換新了。
只是那份腳本從頭到尾沒有人寫「換完要重啟服務」。
它安安靜靜、準時、正確地，每三個月幫我們續期一次，然後什麼也沒發生地過了兩年。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個相信「自動化了就不用管」的同事。最可怕的不是沒自動化，是自動化成功了但少做最後一步。
variations: 延伸：事後檢討結論只有一句——『自動化不等於自動生效。』
也可以接：『那兩年它每三個月都成功一次，只是成功的定義跟我們想的不一樣。』

en.content:
3 a.m. The whole site is down.
Nobody touched the code. Nobody deployed. Nobody went near the database.
Forty minutes of digging later: the certificate expired.
The auto-renewal script? It ran. It ran beautifully. The cert was genuinely renewed.
It just never occurred to anyone to add "now restart the server."
For two years it quietly, punctually, correctly renewed our cert every ninety days — and accomplished absolutely nothing.
en.editorNote: For the coworker who thinks automated means handled. The scary failure isn't the missing script — it's the script that succeeds at the wrong thing.
variations: Extension: the entire postmortem was one line — 'automated is not the same as in effect.'
Follow-up: 'It succeeded every ninety days for two years. Its definition of success just wasn't ours.'

items.sourceNote: 2026 — permission-prompt fatigue leads devs to blanket-approve everything their agent asks for

zh-tw.content:
第一天：agent 每要跑一個指令就問我一次，我認真看完才按同意。
第三天：我只看指令的第一個字。
第五天：我把「以後都不用問了」勾起來。
第九天：它問我要不要清掉一個資料夾，我按了同意。
第九天又過了三秒：我開始回想那個資料夾叫什麼名字。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給任何把 AI 權限開到底的人。點同意點到麻木這件事，我們在 cookie 同意視窗上就練習過很多年了。
variations: 延伸：安全機制的壽命，取決於它問第幾次會被關掉。通常是第七次。
也可以收尾成：『不是我信任它，是我懶得再讀一次。這兩件事在事故報告裡長得一模一樣。』

en.content:
Day 1: the agent asks before every command. I read each one carefully, then approve.
Day 3: I read the first word of the command.
Day 5: I check the box that says "don't ask me again."
Day 9: it asks whether it can clear out a directory. I approve.
Day 9, three seconds later: I start trying to remember what that directory was called.
en.editorNote: For anyone who cranked their agent's permissions wide open. We've been training for this on cookie consent banners for years.
variations: Extension: a safety prompt's lifespan is however many times it can ask before you disable it. Usually seven.
Follow-up: 'I didn't trust it — I just didn't want to read again. In the incident report those look identical.'

items.sourceNote: 2026 hype-cycle meme — low code to no code to AI agents, and the headcount goes up every time

zh-tw.content:
2018 年：low code，讓工程師少寫一點。
2021 年：no code，讓公司不用請工程師。
2024 年：AI 寫程式，工程師這職業要消失了。
2026 年：我們公司歷史上工程師最多的一年。
因為現在有一套沒人寫過、沒人看過、但每天都在收錢的系統，需要有人去理解它。
這年頭最穩的工作，就是負責看懂機器留下來的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個被唱衰過職涯的工程師。每一次「工程師要被取代了」，最後都變成「工程師要負責收拾」。
variations: 延伸：我的職稱還是工程師，工作內容比較接近考古學家。
也可以接：『產生程式碼的成本降到接近零之後，唯一貴的東西變成——有人真的看得懂。』

en.content:
2018: low code — devs write less.
2021: no code — companies don't need devs.
2024: AI writes the code — the job is going away.
2026: largest engineering headcount in our company's history.
Because we now run a system nobody wrote, nobody has read, and that bills customers every single day — and someone has to understand it.
The safest job right now is being the person who can read what the machines left behind.
en.editorNote: For every dev whose career got declared dead. Every 'engineers are being replaced' cycle ends with engineers cleaning it up.
variations: Extension: my title still says engineer. The actual work is closer to archaeology.
Follow-up: 'Once generating code costs nothing, the only expensive thing left is someone who genuinely understands it.'

items.sourceNote: Dependency major-version upgrade pain — changelog claims no breaking changes

zh-tw.content:
更新日誌寫：「本次為主版本更新，無破壞性變更。」
我看了很感動，直接升上去。
編譯錯誤 214 個。
我回去重看那句話，發現它其實沒有騙我——
他們只是覺得「把所有函式改名」不算破壞性變更，那叫「命名一致性優化」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在盯著一整片紅色編譯錯誤的人。看更新日誌要看的不是他們寫了什麼，是他們沒寫什麼。
variations: 延伸：主版本號從 2 跳到 3，只跳了一個數字，我的週末跳了整個。
也可以收尾成：『所謂無破壞性變更，意思是沒有破壞到他們自己那邊。』

en.content:
The changelog said: "Major version bump. No breaking changes."
I was genuinely moved. I upgraded immediately.
214 compile errors.
I went back and reread that line, and honestly? They didn't lie —
they just don't count "renamed every function" as a breaking change. They call it "naming consistency improvements."
en.editorNote: For anyone staring at a wall of red build output. Read a changelog for what it leaves out, not what it says.
variations: Extension: the major version went from 2 to 3. One number. My weekend went considerably further.
Follow-up: 'No breaking changes' means nothing broke on their end.

items.sourceNote: git bisect docs plus the well-known team pain of repo-wide formatting commits polluting bisect and blame (the reason .git-blame-ignore-revs exists)

zh-tw.content:
線上壞了三個禮拜，沒有人知道是從哪一版開始的。
我很得意地祭出 git bisect，二分了十一次，精準抓到第一個壞掉的 commit。
那則 commit 訊息寫：`style: 全專案套用 formatter`。
變更檔案數：兩千一百個。
我一行一行往下看，看到第一千四百多個檔案的時候找到了——有人趁全專案格式化的時候，順手把一個 `>=` 改成了 `>`。
git bisect 幫我從三個禮拜縮小到一個 commit。
然後那個 commit 本身就是一片大海。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在 bisect 的人。也很適合在團隊裡當成溫柔的提醒：格式化請自己開一個 commit，不要夾東西進去。
variations: 延伸：那天之後我們多了一條規定——格式化 commit 裡夾邏輯改動的人，負責值班一個月。
也可以收尾成：『二分搜尋是 O(log n) 沒錯，但前提是每個 commit 都還是人類看得完的尺寸。』

en.content:
Prod had been broken for three weeks and nobody knew which release did it.
So I pulled out git bisect. Eleven steps. It landed precisely on the first bad commit.
Commit message: `style: run the formatter across the repo`.
Files changed: 2,100.
I read them one by one, and somewhere around file 1,400 I found it — while reformatting everything, someone had quietly turned a `>=` into a `>`.
Bisect narrowed three weeks down to a single commit.
That commit was its own ocean.
en.editorNote: For anyone mid-bisect. Also a gentle team reminder: formatting gets its own commit, and nothing rides along with it.
variations: Extension: new team rule after that day — sneak a logic change into a formatting commit, you own the pager for a month.
Follow-up: 'Bisect really is O(log n). It just assumes each commit is still a human-sized amount of reading.'

items.sourceNote: Secrets-management writeups on .env sprawl — dev teams passing unencrypted env files around over Slack, no owner, no rotation, prod credentials mixed in with local ones

zh-tw.content:
新人第一天：「請問本機要跑起來的環境變數，要去哪裡拿？」
資深工程師打開 Slack 往上翻，翻到 2021 年的一則私訊，裡面有一個附件叫 env.txt。
他轉發過去，附註：「這是我學長當年傳給我的，他學長傳給他的。」
新人打開來，裡面四十三個 key。
其中十九個對應的服務早就關掉了。
其中兩個他問遍全公司，沒有人知道是什麼。
其中一個叫 DATABASE_URL，指的是正式環境。
新人跑了 seed script。
那天下午的事故報告標題是：《關於我們的入職文件》。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在幫新人設定本機環境的人。順便問一句：你們公司的 .env 現在到底是誰在管？
variations: 延伸：後來我們終於寫了入職文件。第一行是：『請先到 Slack 搜尋 env.txt。』
也可以接：『傳承是很美的事，但在工程團隊裡通常不是。』

en.content:
New hire, day one: "Where do I get the env vars to run this locally?"
The senior dev opens Slack, scrolls up to a DM from 2021, and finds an attachment named env.txt.
He forwards it, with a note: "This is what the guy before me sent me. He got it from the guy before him."
43 keys.
19 point at services that were shut down years ago.
2 of them nobody in the entire company can identify.
One is called DATABASE_URL. It points at production.
The new hire ran the seed script.
That afternoon's incident report was titled: On The State Of Our Onboarding Docs.
en.editorNote: For whoever is helping a new hire get running locally. Quick question though: who actually owns your .env right now?
variations: Extension: we finally wrote onboarding docs. Line one: 'Search Slack for env.txt.'
Follow-up: 'Inheritance is a beautiful thing. Rarely on an engineering team.'

items.sourceNote: Incident-management writeups: most teams close well under half of their postmortem action items, and vague ones like 'improve monitoring' are the classic never-done entry

zh-tw.content:
打開事故追蹤看板，篩選條件：未完成的 action item。
2023/04　加強監控　　　　負責人：小陳　　狀態：未開始
2023/11　補上告警門檻　　負責人：小陳　　狀態：未開始
2024/06　建立 runbook　　負責人：小陳　　狀態：進行中（進行了兩年）
2025/02　加強監控（重複）負責人：小陳　　狀態：未開始
2026/07　加強監控　　　　負責人：小陳　　狀態：今天剛開的
小陳已經離職一年半了。
這次的根因是：沒有人收到告警。
會議結論：新增一個 action item——加強監控。
zh-tw.editorNote: postmortem 開完之後傳給團隊，效果最好。真正的問題從來不是根因分析寫得不夠深，是沒有人有時間做後面那一段。
variations: 延伸：我們的事故檢討寫得很完整，完整到今年的可以直接複製去年的。
也可以收尾成：『同一條 action item 出現第三次的時候，它就不是 action item 了，那叫公司文化。』

en.content:
Opened the incident tracker. Filter: open action items.
2023-04  Improve monitoring      owner: Chen    status: not started
2023-11  Add alert thresholds    owner: Chen    status: not started
2024-06  Write a runbook        owner: Chen    status: in progress (for two years)
2025-02  Improve monitoring (dup)  owner: Chen    status: not started
2026-07  Improve monitoring      owner: Chen    status: filed today
Chen left the company eighteen months ago.
This week's root cause: nobody got paged.
Meeting outcome: file an action item to improve monitoring.
en.editorNote: Best sent to the team right after a postmortem. The failure was never the analysis — it's that nobody has time for the part that comes after.
variations: Extension: our postmortems are thorough. So thorough that this year's is last year's, copied.
Follow-up: 'The third time the same action item shows up, it isn't an action item anymore. That's culture.'

items.sourceNote: Developer survey coverage: the top frustration (66%) is answers that are almost right but not quite; 45% say debugging that kind of code takes longer than writing it themselves

zh-tw.content:
今年的開發者調查出爐了。
最讓工程師崩潰的第一名，不是編譯錯誤，也不是需求又改。
是那種「看起來完全正確，但就是差那麼一點」的答案。
完全錯的，十秒就抓出來丟掉。
差一點對的，你會相信它、幫它找理由、跟同事辯護它，然後花三個小時證明自己錯了。
修好的那一刻你才算出來：從頭自己寫，四十分鐘。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在團隊頻道當作「今天為什麼沒進度」的官方說明。也很適合傳給那位問「不是都幫你寫好了嗎，怎麼還要這麼久」的主管。
variations: 短版：錯得離譜的答案是敵人，差一點對的答案是內鬼。
也可以收尾成：「我不怕它不會，我怕它會一半。」

en.content:
This year's developer survey is out.
The number one thing that breaks engineers isn't compiler errors, and it isn't changing requirements.
It's the answer that looks completely correct and is off by just a hair.
Something flat-out wrong, you spot in ten seconds and throw away.
Something almost right, you believe. You defend it in review. You invent reasons for it. Then you spend three hours proving yourself wrong.
The moment you finally fix it, you do the math: writing it from scratch would have taken forty minutes.
en.editorNote: Good as the official explanation in your team channel for why today produced nothing. Also good for the manager asking why it still takes so long when the code was 'already written for you.'
variations: Short version: a wildly wrong answer is an enemy. An almost-right answer is a mole.
Alt ending: 'I'm not scared of the ones that can't. I'm scared of the ones that half-can.'

items.sourceNote: 2026 engineering-benchmark reporting: feature-branch throughput up ~59% year over year while median main-branch throughput actually fell — review and approval became the constraint

zh-tw.content:
季度工程報表出來，主管很興奮。
「分支上開出來的 PR，比去年成長五成九。」
他翻到下一頁，笑容停住了。
真正合併進主線的數量，比去年還少。
主管皺眉：「所以瓶頸在哪？」
全組安靜了三秒。資深工程師指了指自己的眼睛。
「這裡。寫程式從來就不是瓶頸，敢按下同意的人才是。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在大家互相催 review、待審清單爆炸的那一週丟到頻道裡。也可以當作「為什麼要限制同時開工數量」的開場白。
variations: 延伸：我們的速度指標很漂亮，漂亮到全部堆在同一個人的待審清單上。
也可以收尾成：「產出翻倍很容易，願意扛責任的人翻倍才難。」

en.content:
The quarterly engineering report lands and the director is thrilled.
"Pull requests opened are up fifty-nine percent year over year."
He flips to the next page and the smile stalls.
The number actually merged into main is down.
"So where's the bottleneck?" he asks.
Three seconds of silence. Then the senior engineer points at her own eyes.
"Here. Writing the code was never the bottleneck. Someone willing to hit approve — that's the bottleneck."
en.editorNote: Drop this in the channel during the week everyone is begging for reviews and the queue is on fire. Also works as the opener for 'why we should cap work in progress.'
variations: Extension: our velocity metrics look gorgeous. So gorgeous they're all piled in one person's review queue.
Alt ending: 'Doubling output is easy. Doubling the people willing to own it is the hard part.'

items.sourceNote: Google SRE book on symptom-based monitoring — the classic failure mode is a shallow health check that only proves the process is alive, not that it is doing anything useful

zh-tw.content:
客服在群組貼上第四十七封客訴的時候，我才打開監控儀表板。
全綠。可用性 99.99%。過去七天零告警。
我盯著那片漂亮的綠色看了很久，然後去翻健康檢查那支端點的程式碼。
它只做一件事：回傳「我還活著」。
它從來沒有問過自己，有沒有在做事。
那一刻我懂了——那不是監控，那是自我肯定。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在有人說「指標明明都正常」的時候拿出來。重點不是嘲諷，是提醒：檢查活著，跟檢查有用，是完全不同的兩件事。
variations: 短版：我們的系統從來沒掛過，掛的是使用者的耐心。
延伸：後來我們加了一支真的會去查資料庫的健康檢查，它上線第一天就紅了三次。

en.content:
Support had posted the forty-seventh complaint in the channel before I finally opened the dashboard.
All green. 99.99% availability. Zero alerts in seven days.
I stared at that beautiful wall of green for a while, then went and read the health check endpoint.
It does exactly one thing: return "I'm alive."
It has never once asked itself whether it's doing any work.
That's when it hit me. That isn't monitoring. That's affirmations.
en.editorNote: Pull this out the next time someone says 'but all the metrics look normal.' The point isn't the dunk — it's that proving you're alive and proving you're useful are two different checks.
variations: Short version: our system has never gone down. What went down was the users' patience.
Extension: we added a health check that actually queries the database. It went red three times on day one.

items.sourceNote: The left-pad unpublish incident — an eleven-line package vanished and builds broke across the ecosystem; still the canonical dependency-fragility story

zh-tw.content:
早上十點十七分，全公司的建置在同一分鐘倒光。
追了兩個小時，兇手是一個十一行的小套件。
作者八年前寫的，上禮拜把整個 repo 刪了，因為他說他很久沒在寫程式了。
我們的金流、後台、客服工具，全部間接依賴它。
那十一行在做什麼？
把字串前面的空白拿掉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在討論要不要鎖版本、要不要自架快取的會議前丟給大家。也很適合回應那句「這種小工具自己寫太浪費時間了吧」。
variations: 延伸：那天下午全組做的第一件事，是把那十一行複製進自己的專案。
也可以收尾成：「現代軟體是一座高塔，塔底有一根牙籤，而牙籤是志工削的。」

en.content:
10:17 a.m. Every build in the company died within the same minute.
Two hours of digging. The culprit was an eleven-line package.
Written eight years ago by one guy who deleted the whole repo last week, because, in his words, he hasn't written code in ages.
Our payments service, our admin panel, our support tooling — all of it depended on him, indirectly.
What do those eleven lines do?
Strip the spaces off the front of a string.
en.editorNote: Send this before the meeting about pinning versions or hosting an internal mirror. Also the perfect reply to 'writing that little helper ourselves would be a waste of time.'
variations: Extension: the first thing the team did that afternoon was paste those eleven lines into our own repo.
Alt ending: 'Modern software is a tower, and somewhere near the bottom is a toothpick, whittled by a volunteer.'

items.sourceNote: The stale-bot action that auto-closes inactive issues — the reason so many searches for a rare error end in an unanswered, auto-closed thread

zh-tw.content:
我把整段錯誤訊息貼進搜尋框。
全世界只有一筆結果。
是三年前的我，在某個專案的 issue 區開的問題。
底下唯一一則回覆來自機器人：「本議題已六十天無人回應，自動關閉。」
我按了重新開啟，在下面留言：「我又來了。」
然後補一句給三年後的自己：「如果你也是搜到這裡——先去看第三個設定檔。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合深夜卡關的時候傳給同事互相取暖。順便提醒一件事：當年那句「之後再補說明」，最後補的人一定是你自己。
variations: 短版：這世上唯一在乎我這個 bug 的人是三年前的我，而他也不知道答案。
延伸：後來我真的把解法寫在那則 issue 底下。隔年有人按了愛心，點開一看，是我自己的另一個帳號。

en.content:
I pasted the whole error message into the search box.
One result. In the entire world.
It was me, three years ago, filing an issue on some project.
The only reply underneath came from a bot: "This issue has had no activity for 60 days and has been closed automatically."
I hit reopen and left a comment: "It's me again."
Then one more, for whoever I am in three years: "If you got here by searching too — check the third config file first."
en.editorNote: Send it to a teammate stuck at 1 a.m. It also carries a quiet reminder: that 'I'll document this later' from years ago? You are the one who ends up documenting it.
variations: Short version: the only person in the world who cared about my bug was me three years ago, and he didn't know either.
Extension: I did eventually post the fix under that issue. A year later someone reacted with a heart. It was my other account.
